articles.title: A New Age of ‘Analog Dressing’ Is Upon Us
articles.summary: Spotted at NYFW: clothes that go off the grid.
articles.body:
Let's take a second to remember what it was like to get dressed before we walked around all day with professional-level cameras in our pockets: We rarely took pictures of ourselves doing mundane tasks—and if there was an impending photo opportunity on the horizon, one couldn't test-shoot a look from multiple mirror selfie angles and instantly send the shots to a friend for opinions. This was not that long ago, and yet, it feels like a wistful epoch of yore, tinged with a dreamy sepia filter in our collective memories. To put on clothes without overanalyzing how one's outfit might be documented in any number of situations that could arise (or, gasp, within a candid snap) is an intoxicating notion, a hall pass to experiment with haphazard layering or forego your steamer.

In a world where having a glossy and meticulously crafted digital persona has become the baseline standard, messy, spontaneous styling equals freedom—and freedom is nothing if not the ultimate luxury. So it only makes sense that some of the biggest brands showing at New York Fashion Week this season have been leaning hard into garments that read as undone and authentically lived in. Blouses with buttons fastened askew at Altuzarra. Sheer tees scrunched and stretched in awkward ways at Brandon Maxwell. Crisp shirting seen at Tommy Hilfiger that appears to be thrown on backward, as if frantically shimmied into after oversleeping. Think of these beautifully imperfect runway moments as the Brick device of the fashion world: sanctioned permission to stop thinking about how your every move might be perceived, and just relax into the physical world. Welcome to the new era of analog dressing.

"These don't really translate in pictures," my editor tells me as she opens her camera roll in a cab between events to show me images of the latest Derek Lam collection , built around artfully folded utilitarian separates and flouncy little dresses. On her six-ish-inch screen, the pieces look weirdly wrinkled and crinkled, as if they had gone straight from the dryer to being slept in all night. In person, though, the creases and shadows are what give them character.

Character is also a descriptor that's always well-applied to Rachel Comey's line, regardless of the current trends. So it's fitting the designer is a shining example of this sort of 20th-century bedroom styling I've noticed permeating the Spring/Summer 2027 shows. Her latest creations were packed with charmingly mussed details that won't necessarily translate to an algorithm's whims: long sleeves casually tied around one's waist, necklines pushed to the side, silky silhouettes that could be neatly ironed, but look cooler when rumpled. The looks at Coach gave a similar impression of being thrown together on the fly, full of tossed-aside blazers knotted at the hips, and extra-long pants puddling over scuffed white sneakers. Meanwhile, even Carolina Herrera—a proper and polished ladies-who-lunch label if there ever was one—incorporated a sweater set with the cardigan secured with a single button shifted over one shoulder as if the wearer couldn't be bothered to find a more flattering way for it lay. The shift was subtle but palpable, and made such sophisticated clothes seem slightly more approachable.

I find many of these runway looks to have same ineffably interesting aura as Jane Birkin with her eponymous structured tote, legendary for the way it was marred with scuffs and covered in stickers and baubles. Or French model-turned-designer Inès de la Fressange, who famously wore the same falling-apart white jeans and blue sweaters when she wasn't on location with houses like Chanel. Essentially, it's the kind of strikingly dissonant visual clutter that you can't look away from in real life, clothes that draw you to someone before they even speak. It's something I've been thinking a lot this week as I run to all corners of the city: how many of the wardrobe choices that have made me do a double take are just non-industry people going about their regular lives. There was the girl grabbing coffee in extra-baggy hip slung jeans and short tweedy jacket over a tank, and the dog walker in a pristine tennis skirt and just-cropped-enough structured sweatshirt, their clothing combinations worn with the ease of a second skin.

Analog dressing, however, is not confined to daytime activities. There's also 7 For All Mankind to consider: The beloved denim behemoth's latest catwalk reflected the sort of cig- and Jägerbomb-tinged throw-on-and-go looks that arise out of partying from midnight straight into work the next morning. With a parade of Hot Mess Express models—an assessment I type with love!—the show was an homage to the give-no-f*cks glamour of early 2000s club culture: dangerously low short-shorts, tottery platform stilettos (or totally bare feet), and long and silly skinny scarfs.

As only those who came of age in that era can tell you, what made it so special was the lack of constant surveillance, thus giving participants the nerve to dance and get into trouble with abandon. It's logical that generations who grew up with multi-step skincare tutorials and matching athleisure sets might want to channel some of that manic movie-quality energy into their own wardrobe. Sure, the haphazardly thrown together nightlife clothes reflect a sense that the wearer is either on their way to or stumbling home from a crash-out, but that's sort of the point: the stakes of losing one's composure in public have never been higher. The idea of doing so without instant documentation is downright liberating.

Does IRL magnetism even matter anymore if it doesn't win you any new followers or likes? This seems to be the question that we're all grappling with as many of us reassess our relationship with technology in this age of filters, everything-maxxing, and AI scandals. The mental load of thinking about how to both live one's life and perform it online for others to consume has become exhausting, a task none of us knew we were taking on when we downloaded our first social media apps in the 2010s.

I know that, at least for me, approaching my wardrobe in the morning has always been a refuge, a way I can control who I'm going to be at least for that day. Sometimes it's armor against judgment; other times it's a representation of my current state of mind. Occasionally, it's a full-blown thirst trap for no particular reason, because life is too short not to dress hot when you're really feeling yourself. In short, I get dressed by way of instinct—and the only time my gut-impulse formula falters is when I start overanalyzing what other people might think, worrying that the outfit I'm gravitating toward might be something I regret on the grid. It comforts me that designers seem to be experiencing the same fatigue, and are now leaning into the kind of fashion that's meant to be worn for one's self in the physical world. It's tangible style at its best, designed to be pulled and twisted and tied throughout the day without overthinking. But will we really wear the best of it all without finding a way to capture every possible angle for posterity? Honestly, I doubt it. But here's hoping that after the shot is secured, these clothes will inspire us to shove our phones deep in our bags and, at least for a little while, dance like no ones recording.

articles.title: Umar Khalid film gets private Kurla screening after Versova cancellation
articles.summary: Private Kurla screening held for Umar Khalid documentary after Versova event was cancelled; activists allege police pressure, amid CBFC certification dispute.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A day after a planned screening of a 2024 documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid was cancelled in Versova following alleged intervention by Mumbai Police, the film was screened at a private event in Kurla on Sunday.More than 20 people attended the invite-only screening at a community centre, where the documentary Prisoner No. 626710 is Present, directed by Lalit Vachnani, was followed by a reading of poetry by Gulfisha Fatima, a co-accused with Khalid in the 2020 Delhi riots case.The Versova screening had been organised by Mumbai-based activist-influencers Prashant Purandir and Shrishti Khanna. They alleged that people in civilian clothes claiming to be police first approached the venue manager and pressured him to cancel the event. They said the manager subsequently received a call from the superintendent of police and that a police vehicle later arrived at the venue.“We were not given any reason or told that police permission was required,” Purandir and Khanna said, alleging that the intervention amounted to intimidation. They also claimed that a Bandra venue they had earlier considered was “threatened” and that several other venues declined to host the screening after learning that the film was about Khalid.The documentary has also faced cancellations elsewhere. A planned screening at NLSIU, Bengaluru, on Sept 14 was postponed and later scrapped following objections from ABVP, while a screening at IIIT-Hyderabad scheduled for Sept 18 was cancelled after Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) said on X that the event would be “in violation of the Cinematograph Act”.Bombay HC lawyer Chandni Chawla said CBFC certification requirements apply to public or commercial screenings and that private screenings are not governed by the Cinematograph Act.The Kurla organiser, Abhishek, said he was advised not to publicise the event as a precaution and kept it invite-only and free of charge. “That way no one could argue that the screening was public and so the film requires certification. The film is not banned. It’s ridiculous that we should be made to feel afraid to watch it,” he said.The documentary covers the events preceding Khalid’s arrest and his incarceration. articles.title: Home Guard aspirant dies during physical test; 3rd death in a week in  UP
articles.summary: Home Guard aspirant Shivam Yadav, 27, died after collapsing during a PET run in Moradabad; third death in a week in western UP recruitment drive.
articles.body: MEERUT: A 27-year-old Home Guard aspirant from Bareilly died after collapsing during a physical efficiency test (PET) at the 9th Battalion PAC ground in Moradabad on Friday, marking the third death in the ongoing recruitment drive in western Uttar Pradesh within a week.Shivam Yadav, a resident of Bareilly city, fell unconscious about 50m from the finish line while running the 12th and final lap of the mandatory 4.8-km race. He was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead, officials said.His father, Vinod Yadav, said he reached the ground after learning that his son’s condition had deteriorated mid-race but was stopped at the gate by police personnel and alleged that he was not allowed inside despite repeated pleas. “By the time I was let in, Shivam had already collapsed,” he said.Shivam’s wife, Komal, said the family had not imagined that the test would cost him his life. The couple had been married for five years and have a toddler daughter.A BTech and BEd graduate who had also cleared the UP-Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), Shivam ran a coaching centre. He had cleared the preliminary and main examinations for railway loco pilot recruitment and was awaiting the results of the Lekhpal and Railway Group D examinations, his family said.He is survived by his parents, wife, daughter and three brothers.In Meerut, two other aspirants died in a similar fashion earlier this week. Shamli resident Ankuj Malik, 39, collapsed on Tuesday after his condition deteriorated following the PET at Kailash Prakash Sports Stadium. Another aspirant, Tarun Kumar, also died this week after falling ill during the run. All three candidates were suspected to have died of cardiac arrest.Meanwhile, two candidates at Bareilly’s Dorilal Stadium — Surjeet Singh and Yuvraj — were hospitalised on Saturday after one collapsed and the other sustained a leg injury, officials said.Neither Moradabad nor Meerut police have shared any details in the three cases. Attempts to reach Moradabad SSP Satpal Antil and Meerut SSP BBGTS Murthy for comment were unsuccessful.Stay updated with the latest Bareilly news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Transformadores pegam fogo e deixam moradores sem energia na Asa Sul, em Brasília | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Neoenergia, uma tentativa de furto de cabos causou um curto-circuito na subestação da 311 Sul.
articles.summary: Segundo a Neoenergia, uma tentativa de furto de cabos causou um curto-circuito na subestação da 311 Sul.
articles.body:
Dois transformadores pegaram fogo em uma subestação de energia na 311 Sul, em Brasília , e deixaram moradores da região sem energia na madrugada desta segunda-feira (21). Ninguém ficou ferido e, por isso, não será solicitado perícia.

Imagens feitas por moradores mostram as chamas, por volta das 3h da manhã ( veja vídeo acima ).

Segundo a Neoenergia, concessionária que faz o fornecimento de energia, uma tentativa de furto de cabos causou um curto-circuito na subestação . Na 312 Sul, a energia foi retomada por volta das 6h30.

Funcionários da Neoenergia explicam que – apesar de todas as quadras da Asa Sul terem uma subestação de energia – o circuito que faz a ligação do abastecimento é interligado. Por isso, até a 109 Sul foi afetada.

Transformadores pegam fogo e deixam moradores sem energia no DF — Foto: Reprodução

"Informamos que uma tentativa de furto de cabos provocou um curto-circuito em uma Estação Transformadora, causando a interrupção pontual no fornecimento de energia na região. O incidente provocou um incêndio que danificou severamente a estrutura e diversos equipamentos.

Equipes da Neoenergia já estão no local e trabalham, de forma ininterrupta, em um serviço de alta complexidade para substituir os equipamentos danificados e restabelecer o fornecimento de energia com a maior brevidade possível."

articles.title: Acidente no Hopi Hari: vídeo mostra jovem antes de lesão na Montezum | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação apura como Júlia sofreu traumatismo craniano, deixando sequelas após movimentos bruscos da atração.
articles.summary: Investigação apura como Júlia sofreu traumatismo craniano na Montezum, deixando sequelas após movimentos bruscos da atração.
articles.body:
Imagens exibidas pelo Fantástico mostram momentos antes de uma jovem sair desacordada de uma montanha-russa no Hopi Hari, em Vinhedo (SP ). Segundo a família, Júlia Rimoli sofreu um traumatismo cranioencefálico após andar na Montezum, uma das atrações mais conhecidas do parque. O acidente deixou a vítima com sequelas neurológicas e passou a ser investigado pelo Ministério Público de São Paulo.

Júlia estava acompanhada do marido, João Pedro. Registros feitos pelo próprio casal mostram o momento em que os dois embarcam na montanha-russa pela primeira vez. Apesar de apreensivos, eles fizeram o passeio sem intercorrências.

"A gente foi a primeira vez, não teve problema", relata João Pedro.

Imagens mostram últimos momentos de jovem antes de sair desacordada de montanha-russa no Hopi Hari — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

No fim da tarde, João Pedro se lembrou de que tinha direito a uma promoção. Os dois decidiram voltar à montanha-russa.

"Não ia pegar nem fila. A gente falou, então vamos antes de ir embora. E foi aí que começou todo o pesadelo".

As câmeras do parque registraram o momento em que Júlia e João Pedro se sentam em um dos bancos de trás do carrinho. Na subida, Júlia aparece consciente e tranquila. Não há imagens do restante do percurso.

Cerca de dois minutos depois, o carrinho retorna à plataforma. Júlia está desacordada.

"Ela já estava inconsciente, já estava convulsionando e nesse momento você fica desesperado, não sabe o que fazer".

Imagens mostram últimos momentos de jovem antes de sair desacordada de montanha-russa do Hopi Hari — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Os registros mostram funcionários se aproximando do carrinho após a chegada à estação. Cerca de seis minutos depois, a jovem é retirada em uma maca e levada para atendimento médico.

"Levaram ela para o ambulatório do próprio Hopi Hari. Foi uma uma cena de terror. Ela ficou inconsciente o tempo todo", diz o marido de Júlia.

Em seguida, a atração voltou a funcionar normalmente.

Imagens mostram últimos momentos de jovem antes de acidente em montanha-russa do Hopi Hari — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A vítima foi encaminhada inicialmente ao ambulatório do parque e depois transferida para a Santa Casa de Vinhedo. Exames apontaram uma hemorragia intracraniana e um edema cerebral, quadro que exigiu uma cirurgia de emergência. Ela permaneceu internada por 57 dias.

De acordo com laudo médico citado pela família, o traumatismo foi provocado por um mecanismo de contragolpe durante o percurso na montanha-russa. O documento aponta que movimentos bruscos de aceleração, desaceleração e rotação podem causar rompimento de vasos sanguíneos cerebrais.

Cinco meses após o acidente, a jovem segue em processo de reabilitação. Segundo familiares, ela perdeu os movimentos do lado esquerdo do corpo, enfrenta dificuldades de fala e já passou por sete cirurgias desde o episódio.

O Ministério Público de São Paulo abriu uma investigação para apurar as circunstâncias do caso e determinou a realização de uma perícia na atração. O procedimento ainda está em andamento.

Jovem perde movimentos após andar em montanha-russa do Hopi Hari; MP investiga — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

"A Montezum possui certificação internacional emitida pelo Grupo TUV Nord, uma das maiores organizações de inspeção e testes de atrações do mundo. As inspeções acontecem anualmente no caso de atrações radicais como a Montezum, e bianuais, em atrações de baixa complexidade. Outros importantes protocolos de segurança, treinamento de pessoal e de atenção ao visitante fazem parte da rotina diária do Hopi Hari em todas as suas atrações. O parque também segue rigorosamente a norma nacional para parques de diversões 'ABNT NBR 15926-2023 Equipamentos de Parques de Diversão'.

Antes mesmo de acessar a Montezum, placas contendo dados sobre a atração estão colocadas em pontos de fácil visualização para que todos os visitantes tenham informações claras e detalhadas sobre o funcionamento da montanha russa, além de recomendações e restrições. Ainda quando estão na fila para acessar a atração, um sistema de áudio destaca as recomendações e restrições. E, no momento do embarque, os operadores da atração também reforçam as informações, por meio de um sistema de som. Os procedimentos seguem normas internacionais adotadas em atrações ao redor do mundo e integram rotinas obrigatórias de segurança e operação. De janeiro de 2026 até o momento, mais de 870 mil pessoas frequentaram o parque e, deste total, aproximadamente 470 mil pessoas passaram pela atração, que é a mais visitada do Hopi Hari.

Também é importante destacar que, recentemente, o Ministério Público emitiu parecer sobre a atração enfatizando não haver risco coletivo, defeito no projeto da montanha russa ou qualquer negligência. No texto do parecer, o MP destaca "a regularidade do funcionamento da atração "Montezum" sob a ótica da tutela coletiva e difusa da segurança e saúde dos consumidores". O parecer acrescenta, ainda, que "o estabelecimento prestador do serviço adota protocolos rigorosos de prevenção, manutenção e segurança operacional".

E enfatiza que 'a montanha-russa Montezum é submetida a rotinas periódicas de inspeção técnica diária , abrangendo a estrutura de madeira, trilhos, fixações, travas de segurança, cintos, sensores fotoelétricos, painéis elétricos e sistemas de frenagem, com supervisão por equipe de engenharia e certificações técnicas pertinentes. Ademais, constata-se a existência de sinalização visual e sonora no local, informando previamente a classificação da atração como radical, as forças e movimentos nela envolvidos, além das expressas contra indicações de uso a pessoas com problemas na coluna, gestantes e portadores de condições clínicas específicas', descreve o parecer. As placas indicativas com as informações nelas contidas, também estão anexadas neste email.

O Hopi Hari esclarece ainda que a visitante do Paraná acessou a atração por duas vezes no mesmo dia de sua visita ao parque, conforme imagens anexadas. A primeira ida à Montezum ocorreu às 11h da manhã e a segunda, cerca de cinco horas depois, por volta de 16h30 do mesmo dia.

O episódio envolvendo a jovem paranaense ocorreu em sua segunda passagem pela atração, quando apresentou um quadro de convulsão e recebeu pronto atendimento das equipes do parque, seguindo todos os protocolos de segurança. A providência inicial foi prestar os primeiros socorros no ambulatório do parque. A visitante foi encaminhada para a Santa Casa de Vinhedo, onde permaneceu internada até apresentar condições de retorno à sua cidade. A direção do parque acompanhou de perto o tratamento prestado, sempre em contato com os familiares, custeando as despesas durante a permanência em Vinhedo.

Vale ressaltar que o departamento jurídico do Hopi Hari também manteve contato com os familiares da visitante paranaense para o suporte necessário durante todo o processo de atendimento da paciente em seu tratamento. O corpo jurídico, assim como a direção do parque, seguem à disposição da família da visitante. Importante destacar também que o Hopi Hari dispõe de um seguro que foi franqueado à família.

O Hopi Hari segue investindo em normas, procedimentos e treinamentos visando a segurança das atrações do parque que, nos últimos 5 anos, já recebeu mais de 5,5 milhões de visitantes.

Sobre as ocorrências mencionadas de anos anteriores, esclarecemos que os dados pertencem a gestões passadas. A atual administração tem seu foco estrito na rigorosa cultura de segurança implementada nos últimos 5 anos, responsável por receber mais de 5,5 milhões de visitantes de forma segura.

Normas que seguimos e que regem as inspeções que seguimos 100%.

• Decisão Normativa 52, de 25 de agosto de 1994, do CONFEA. • Ato Normativo nº 02, de 14 de dezembro de 2001, CREA-SP. • ABNT NBR 15926:2023, Equipamentos de Parques de Diversão. • ABNT NBR 16071:2012, “Playgrounds”. • ABNT NBR 5410:vigente, Instalações Elétricas de Baixa Tensão. • ABNT NBR 9050, Acessibilidade a Edificações, Mobiliário, Espaços equipamentos urbanos. • ABNT NBR ISO 21101:2014, Turismo de Aventura – Sistema de Gestão de Segurança – Requisitos. • NR 10 - Segurança em Instalações e Serviços em Eletricidade. • NR 13 - Caldeiras, Vasos de Pressão e Tubulações.

Equipe técnica que trabalha dedicada, na atração

• 1 técnico em mecânica (média de 5h por dia) • 1 técnico em elétrica (média de 2h por dia) • 12 carpinteiros (média de 7h por dia)

• Não foram analisadas somente documentação, tivemos inspeções e avaliações técnicas dos engenheiros do CAEx para elaboração dos pareceres.

• Preventiva diária (realizada diariamente antes da abertura do parque) • 5-6 horas de trabalho realizado por um técnico em mecânica • 1-2 horas de trabalho realizado por um técnico em elétrica • 3-4 horas de trabalho realizado pela equipe de carpintaria (3-4 pessoas) • Preventiva semanal (realizada toda semana nos dias de parque fechado) • 6-7 horas de trabalho realizado por um técnico em mecânica • 2-3 horas de trabalho realizado por um técnico em elétrica • 14-15 horas de trabalho realizado pela equipe de carpintaria (8-9 pessoas) • Preventiva mensal (realizado durante o mês em que foi gerada, conforme programação) • 4-6 horas de trabalho realizado por um técnico em mecânica • 2-3 horas de trabalho realizado por um técnico em elétrica • Anual (realizada nos trens após 1800-2000 horas de trabalho ou a cada dois anos) • 30-50 dias de trabalho realizado pela equipe mecânica (2 mecânicos+1 supervisor)

Sobre o registro de 40 reclamações de visitantes

Em resposta ao questionamento da reportagem, cabe destacar a devida proporcionalidade dos dados: o registro de cerca de 40 reclamações na plataforma Reclame Aqui ao longo dos últimos dois anos refere-se a um universo de aproximadamente 1,2 milhão de visitantes que passaram pela Montezum no mesmo período — o que demonstra um índice estatístico irrisório e abaixo da média mundial, diante do expressivo volume de operações da atração.

Em recente manifestação a respeito do assunto, o Ministério Público deu parecer onde destaca que "o histórico operacional demonstra que eventuais queixas de desconforto muscular constituem episódios isolados, inerentes ao impacto físico esperado em equipamentos de tal natureza, sem qualquer padrão de defeito sistêmico no brinquedo ou falha na prestação do serviço", diz o parecer.

Os casos relatados são encaminhados ao SAV (Serviço de Atendimento ao Visitante) que trata com atenção os relatos de queixas sobre lesões ou desconfortos físicos, passíveis em uma atração amplamente anunciada como radical, mantendo contato com o reclamante para inicialmente ouvir seu relato e seguir se necessário com o acompanhamento."

articles.summary: Felipe Camarão será o último entrevistado da série do JMTV1 com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026; g1 Maranhão transmite ao vivo.
articles.body:
Felipe Camarão (PT) — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Felipe Camarão ( PT ) participa nesta segunda-feira (21) da série de entrevistas do JMTV 1ª Edição com os candidatos ao Governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026. A conversa será exibida ao vivo pela TV Mirante, durante o telejornal, que começa às 11h45, com transmissão também pelo g1 Maranhão .

O candidato do PT é o último a participar da série de entrevistas, que começou no dia 14 de setembro.

O JMTV 1ª Edição começa às 11h45 . A entrevista com o candidato será exibida ao vivo durante o telejornal e terá duração de 30 minutos. O público também poderá acompanhar a transmissão pelo g1 Maranhão. A conversa será conduzida pelos jornalistas Tayse Feques e Rodrigo Bomfim .

Durante a entrevista, o candidato responderá a perguntas elaboradas por 32 estudantes maranhenses , que representarão os eleitores durante a dinâmica . Os estudantes ficarão posicionados atrás do candidato e dos apresentadores.

articles.title: Tempestade no Paraná: cidades em alerta vermelho e ventos 100km/h | G1
articles.standfirst: Alerta vale para municípios do extremo Oeste. Temporais ganham força entre a tarde e a noite desta segunda-feira (21).
articles.summary: A tempestade no Paraná coloca o extremo Oeste em alerta vermelho nesta segunda (21), com ventos de 100 km/h e risco de granizo em 55 municípios.
articles.body:
Cinquenta e cinco cidades do extremo Oeste do Paraná estão sob alerta vermelho, de grande perigo, para tempestades nesta segunda-feira (21), segundo o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet). Confira quais abaixo.

O aviso é válido até 23h59 e prevê chuva superior a 60 milímetros por hora ou acima de 100 milímetros no dia, ventos acima de 100 km/h e queda de granizo.

O alerta indica grande risco de danos em edificações, corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de árvores, alagamentos e transtornos no transporte rodoviário.

Ao mesmo tempo, outras 348 cidades do Paraná estão sob alerta laranja, de perigo, para tempestades. O aviso prevê chuva de 30 a 60 milímetros por hora ou até 100 milímetros no dia, ventos de 60 a 100 km/h e queda de granizo. O risco de danos é considerado menor que no alerta vermelho, mas ainda inclui possibilidade de corte de energia, estragos em plantações, queda de árvores e alagamentos.

Segundo o Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar), o tempo começa estável em grande parte do estado, mas a situação muda ao longo do dia com o avanço de uma frente fria. Confira previsão do tempo abaixo.

temporal tempestade chuva nuvens paraná pr — Foto: Jonathan Campos/AEN

Previsão do tempo segunda-feira (21), no Paraná — Foto: Simepar

De acordo com Samuel Braun, meteorologista do Simepar, uma frente fria avança pela região Sul do Brasil nesta segunda-feira. Ao mesmo tempo, um sistema de baixa pressão entre o norte da Argentina e o Paraguai favorece a entrada de umidade e calor da região amazônica.

A combinação deixa a atmosfera instável e favorece a formação de áreas de chuva e tempestades.

No Paraná, as primeiras instabilidades devem atingir Oeste, Sudoeste e Sul ainda pela manhã, com chuva irregular. Entre a tarde e a noite, a previsão indica uma maior organização das áreas de instabilidade, aumentando o risco de tempestades em boa parte do estado.

"Entre a tarde e a noite, a organização da instabilidade é maior, proporcionando a ocorrência de tempestades, algumas severas, em boa parte do estado", afirmou Braun.

Apesar da mudança no tempo, o Paraná começa a segunda-feira com temperaturas mais elevadas em algumas áreas.

As máximas devem passar dos 30°C no Noroeste, Norte e Litoral. No início do dia, os termômetros variam em torno de 25°C no Oeste, 17°C em Curitiba e 20°C no Litoral.

Previsão do tempo para terça-feira (22), no Paraná — Foto: Simepar

Na terça-feira (22), o Paraná continua sob influência do avanço da frente fria e o tempo permanece instável.

O risco de tempestades é maior entre as regiões Leste e Noroeste. Ainda há possibilidade de chuva fraca em alguns setores, mas a previsão indica melhora das condições a partir da tarde.

Em caso de tempestade, o Inmet recomenda desligar aparelhos elétricos e o quadro geral de energia.

Em situações de enxurrada, documentos e objetos de valor devem ser colocados em sacos plásticos.

Se houver confirmação de uma situação de grande perigo, a orientação é procurar abrigo e evitar permanecer ao ar livre.

A população pode acompanhar os alertas da Defesa Civil pelo telefone 199 e do Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193 . Também é possível receber alertas meteorológicos da Defesa Civil por SMS . Para isso, basta enviar o CEP para o número 40199.

O alerta vermelho do Inmet é válido das 0h às 23h59 desta segunda-feira (21) e abrange 55 cidades do extremo Oeste do Paraná.

articles.title: Cães da raça chihuahua são parte coiotes, e talvez por isso sejam 'pequenos, mas bravos' | G1
articles.standfirst: Descoberta destaca a incrível diversidade entre as raças de cães e a força da seleção artificial feita pelos humanos.
articles.summary: Descoberta destaca a incrível diversidade entre as raças de cães e a força da seleção artificial feita pelos humanos.
articles.body:
Uma das menores raças de cães, o chihuahua, tem parte de coiote selvagem em sua composição genética, mostra uma pesquisa publicada recentemente. Os chihuahuas são originários do México, mas hoje a raça é um dos cães de companhia populares em diversos países do mundo, como Reino Unido e EUA.

Os genes do coiote podem ter sido introduzidos acidentalmente nos ancestrais do chihuahua. Mas também podem ser resultado de tentativas deliberadas de cruzar os dois animais – talvez há muitas gerações.

Os coiotes são uma espécie canina selvagem, ligeiramente menor que o lobo cinzento, nativa da América do Norte. A presença de genes de coiote no chihuahua, muito menor, destaca a incrível diversidade dos cães domésticos e suas histórias variadas.

Os coiotes são selvagens e territoriais. E qualquer pessoa que já tenha convivido com um chihuahua sabe que estes pequenos animais podem ter grandes personalidades caninas.

Os chihuahuas são o arquétipo dos cães “pequenos, mas bravos”: ousados, independentes, ágeis, mas também capazes de obediência. Eles não são aqueles cachorrinhos de colo pequenos e sedentários. E essas descobertas podem explicar, em parte, o motivo.

O estudo recente explorou marcas genéticas antigas nos genomas de cães e humanos para validar a eficácia de novas técnicas genéticas. O genoma é o conjunto completo de DNA nas células vivas.

Os pesquisadores demonstraram seus métodos em raças de cães com ligações com as Américas, como o chihuahua e outra raça mexicana, o xoloitzcuintli (frequentemente abreviado para xolo). O xolo é tipicamente caracterizado pela ausência de pelos e por uma personalidade frequentemente distante.

Muitos cães nas Américas hoje são descendentes de raças europeias, um resultado da colonização a partir do século XV. Mas pesquisas anteriores mostraram que o chihuahua e o xolo preservam uma pequena quantidade de ascendência – 4% no chihuahua e 3% no xolo – de cães pré-contato, aqueles que viviam nas Américas antes da chegada dos europeus.

A análise genética do xolo no estudo recente sugere que cães europeus e pré-colombianos estavam se misturando por volta de 1700. Isso está de acordo com evidências que sugerem que europeus e populações indígenas se misturaram por volta da mesma época no México antigo.

Pesquisadores já haviam encontrado evidências da ascendência do coiote no DNA de restos mortais de antigos cães domésticos das Américas. Isso nos lembra que os cães não estão tão distantes de outras espécies de canídeos e podem cruzar com elas com sucesso.

Verificou-se que coiotes e lobos selvagens se hibridizam naturalmente, especialmente em áreas geográficas onde traços comportamentais “semelhantes aos do lobo” são benéficos. Houve até mesmo um relato recente de um híbrido de cão com raposa identificado no Brasil.

Ainda não está claro quando exatamente os genes do coiote entraram na linhagem do chihuahua. As histórias precisas das diferentes raças de cães são difíceis de reconstruir, pois muitas vezes faltam evidências documentais detalhadas.

Então, como o chihuahua acabou ficando tão pequeno, apesar desses genes de coiote? Essa questão deve ser vista sob a ótica da reprodução seletiva, na qual os humanos escolhem diferentes cães para reprodução com base nas características que preferem.

Análises genéticas revelam que quase todas as raças de cães pequenos compartilham uma mutação no gene do fator de crescimento semelhante à insulina 1 (IGF1), que afeta o crescimento celular e, consequentemente, o tamanho corporal. A seleção de cães pequenos com essa mutação parece ter ocorrido bem no início da domesticação canina.

Há algumas evidências da presença de cães de porte pequeno entre as culturas mesoamericanas pré-contato, mas não se sabe como eles se relacionam com os chihuahuas.

Alguns cães, como o cão-lobo tchecoslovaco, parecem visivelmente mais com seus parentes canídeos selvagens e ancestrais, como o lobo cinzento. Eles têm orelhas eretas, corpos musculosos e atléticos e pelagem que proporciona camuflagem e proteção contra condições ambientais extremas.

Outros cães apresentam variações extremas: características exageradas, como costas longas ou pernas curtas. Em alguns casos, essas características físicas trazem consequências significativas para a saúde e o bem-estar dos animais.

O tamanho corporal geral é particularmente variável nos cães, com uma diferença de 40 vezes entre diferentes raças e tipos. Imagine o minúsculo chihuahua ao lado de um imponente grande danês, por exemplo.

Existem também diferenças importantes no comportamento. Se você deseja conviver harmoniosamente com um cão, ou treiná-lo ou utilizá-lo em uma atividade específica, é importante reconhecer isso. De fato, atender às necessidades físicas, psicológicas e emocionais de cada cão é essencial tanto para o bem-estar do animal quanto para o do ser humano, bem como para o sucesso do treinamento.

Assim como no caso da aparência, a seleção natural e a seleção induzida pelo ser humano se combinaram para influenciar essas características. Isso produziu gerações de cães com características comportamentais específicas.

O cão foi um dos primeiros animais a ser domesticado pelos humanos – os exemplos mais antigos têm mais de 15.000 anos. Eles também são uma das espécies domesticadas de maior sucesso.

Os cães são encontrados em todos os continentes, exceto na Antártica, e estima-se que a população global de cães gire entre 700 milhões e 1 bilhão. Eles existem integrados à sociedade humana ou vivendo à margem dela.

Ao longo da história, deve ter ocorrido uma seleção natural de cães com características que conferem vantagens de sobrevivência. Ao mesmo tempo, os seres humanos selecionaram cães individuais com base em atributos desejados, levando ao desenvolvimento de raças e às classificações que vemos em todo o mundo.

Além de ampliar nossa capacidade de explorar a ancestralidade genética das espécies, o estudo mais recente acrescenta detalhes à nossa compreensão de como e quando o cão doméstico evoluiu e se tornou tão diverso.

Isso também pode significar que passemos a pensar menos no “lobo em nossas salas” e mais no “coiote em nossos chihuahuas”.

Além de sua afiliação acadêmica à Nottingham Trent University (NTU) e do apoio do Instituto para a Prática de Intercâmbio de Conhecimento (IKEP) da NTU, Jacqueline Boyd é afiliada ao The Royal Kennel Club (Reino Unido) como associada, atuando como consultora do Grupo Consultivo de Saúde e membro do Comitê de Atividades. Jacqueline é membro titular da Associação de Treinadores de Cães de Estimação (APDT #01583). Ela também escreve, presta consultoria e atua como coach em assuntos caninos de forma independente.

articles.title: 4 men putting up CCTV cameras die after dumper hits crane, auto in southeast Delhi; 2 injured
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Four people installing CCTV cameras for Delhi Traffic Police were killed and two were injured when a dumper truck collided with a stationar.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Four people installing CCTV cameras for Delhi Traffic Police were killed and two were injured when a dumper truck collided with a stationary crane and a parked autorickshaw in Sarita Vihar early Sunday morning.The deceased were identified as Umesh (23), Praveen (35), Suraj (34) and Anup (26). They were residents of Sangam Vihar and Munirka. Two others, Akash (20) and Khem Singh (40), suffered injuries and are under treatment. A seventh person on the spot, identified as Sudhir, was unhurt. The six were taken to a nearby hospital but four of them succumbed to injuries.Police said that on Road No. 13 in Sarita Vihar at 3.20am, the dumper coming from Noida rammed into the crane and a parked autorickshaw while the workers were busy with the installation.Of the four deceased, Suraj worked as an HR manager in the private firm. Praveen was a technician in the same firm and Anup too was an employee. Umesh was an autorickshaw driver.Akash and Khem Singh were also working for the same company. Praveen, Anup and Akash were cousins.A response was also sought from the firm which had assigned the six to carry out the CCTV installation, but it is yet to come.The dumper driver fled and has not yet been traced. Searches are on to arrest him. The vehicle bore a Haryana registration number.A relative of Umesh alleged that there were inadequate safety measures in place for the workers installing the CCTV cameras.An inquiry has revealed that seven people were on the spot. Two workers were standing on the crane and installing the cameras, while two others were standing nearby. One person was inside an autorickshaw and another was standing beside it. The seventh person, Sudhir, was standing some distance away.According to the families of the deceased workers, the people present at the spot had seen the approaching dumper and waved to indicate that the driver must stop, but he did not heed their signal.Police also found out that 50 metres ahead of the spot, there was a fluorescent barricade placed to indicate that work was going on, but the dumper driver did not heed that either.When the dumper hit the crane, the two workers who were fixing the cameras fell down. The impact was so severe that the crane’s tyres burst. The autorickshaw too was damaged.Praveen’s brother, Brijesh, said that while the two workers were fixing the cameras, Praveen was using a laptop to monitor and adjust the cameras. The road where the accident took place was busy and heavy vehicles frequently passed through the stretch at a high speed during the night.The families of the victims learnt about the tragedy from various sources. Some of them got phone calls. articles.title: Planning a trip to Canada: Immigration agency answers the visa questions travellers often get wrong
articles.summary: Tech News News: Canada’s immigration authority has stepped in to clear up some of the most common confusion facing travellers. IRCC shared a post of social media plat.
articles.body: Canada’s immigration authority has stepped in to clear up some of the most common confusion facing travellers. IRCC shared a post of social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) publishing a set of answers to the questions it says that visitors ask most often and the responses are worth a read before you book that trip. With millions of people visiting Canada every year, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) says a handful of questions come up again and again. Here's what the agency wants every prospective visitor to know.Canada’s immigration agency answered some common questionsHow long will a visitor visa actually take?This is where many travellers get caught out. If you do need a visitor visa, you'll have to submit an application along with supporting documents proving your identity, travel plans, and eligibility to enter Canada — and processing times can vary significantly depending on demand and your location. IRCC is urging applicants to check current estimated processing times before applying, rather than assuming last year's timeline still holds.What documents do you need?At a minimum, your application needs a digital copy of your passport or travel document, and it must remain valid for at least six months beyond your planned travel date — a detail that trips up more travellers than you'd expect. The good news: applying online generates a personalised document checklist inside the portal, so you know exactly what's required for your specific case rather than guessing.Can you work or study while visiting?Here's the one that catches people out the most. Visitors are not permitted to work or study in Canada unless they're specifically authorized to do so. If your trip involves any work or study plans, a standard visitor visa or eTA won't cut it — you'll likely need a separate work permit or study permit, and IRCC recommends checking eligibility for either well before you travel.Read IRCC complete post hereMillions of people visit Canada every year. Here are some of the top questions about visiting Canada, answered! 1. Do I need a visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA) to travel to Canada? To visit Canada, most people need a visitor visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA), depending on their citizenship, their travel document and the way they plan to travel to Canada. articles.title: Uttarakhand MBBS scam: Fake certificates showed 'AI-generated pic' of freedom fighter
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: A seven-member special investigation team (SIT) of Dehradun district police unit probing the alleged irregularities in MBBS admissions under.
articles.body: DEHRADUN: A seven-member special investigation team (SIT) of Dehradun district police unit probing the alleged irregularities in MBBS admissions under the freedom-fighter dependents quota in Uttarakhand, has found that the certificates submitted by at least four students of unrelated families carried an AI-generated photograph of late freedom fighter Dharamveer, who was a resident of Dehradun's Jhanda Bazar area.Dehradun SP (rural) Jaya Baluni told TOI on Sunday, "While examining documents submitted by the four students, who availed admission under the freedom fighters' dependents quota in 2025, it was found that the photograph on the freedom fighter certificate was generated with the help of Artificial Intelligence... While the photo resembled the deceased, the other details including his father's name were incorrect." Baluni is leading the SIT set up by Dehradun SSP Pramendra Dobal on Sept 18 after the irregularities surfaced.She further said that police found that all the four students had mentioned "Dharamveer as their paternal and maternal grandfather". "This, in spite of the fact that all four belonged to totally unrelated families who had no connection with him. Also, the mandatory personal details including address and mobile number mentioned in the admission forms by the four students were found to be non-existent. They had mentioned the same mobile number on their forms, which was unusual," added Baluni.All the four students are already facing FIRs registered in the city's Clement Town and Raipur police stations, but are yet to be summoned for questioning as the contact details were found to be fake.Following the findings, police had on Saturday called the late freedom fighter's son and grandson for questioning in the case. Police said they had no idea how his certificate was used; they said he died 12 years ago and, when alive, Dharamveer had instructed authorities not to transfer his pension to anyone after his death, and that even his direct family members had never claimed any benefit using his certificate. "We have asked the SDM office to provide us with related documents for examination," Baluni said, adding that "they now suspect an organised gang to be behind this crime."Another police officer, part of the SIT probe, said that the involvement of officials in the local administration as well as the management of medical colleges and universities was also suspected."It is questionable how those fake freedom fighter dependent certificates were issued on forged documents by govt offices. At the same time, questions arise on the verification done by the college/university management of the documents submitted by the students as all the four had mentioned the same person as their grandfather with fake mobile numbers and addresses. We'll soon question them too," said the officer, who did not wish to be named.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Days after Michael Dell briefly became world’s second richest man, he is selling 4,100-sq-ft Boston penthouse that he purchased 10 years ago for $10.9 million
articles.summary: Tech News News: Just days after Michael Dell briefly climbed to the position of the world’s second-richest man, the Dell Technologies founder is making headlines agai.
articles.body: Just days after Michael Dell briefly climbed to the position of the world’s second-richest man, the Dell Technologies founder is making headlines again — this time in real estate. Dell has put his 4,100-square-foot Boston penthouse on the market, a property he purchased a decade ago for $10.9 million. Located in Boston’s Millennium Tower, the penthouse offers sweeping city views, luxury finishes, and access to exclusive amenities. The residence reflects Dell’s penchant for high-value real estate investments, complementing his portfolio that includes properties in Texas and Hawaii. The listing comes amid Dell’s extraordinary financial year, with his net worth surging by more than $80 billion thanks to booming demand for AI infrastructure.Michael Dell’s almost untouched luxury homeDell bought the Millennium Tower penthouse in 2016 through an LLC. Nearly a decade later, the roughly 4,100-square-foot, three-bedroom unit is heading to a sealed-bid auction with a reserve price $4.4 million below what he originally paid — a potential 41% discount from its last sale price. Bidding is open now and closes on October 29, though the property remains subject to a prior sale.Perched on the 59th floor of Millennium Tower, the penthouse comes with sweeping views and, according to the listing agent, has barely been lived in since Dell bought it. Notably, the home's oven has apparently never even been turned on.The sale comes at an interesting moment for Dell. His fortune took a $15.1 billion hit this past week as Dell Technologies shares fell amid a broader AI-stock selloff, knocking him down to No. 4 on Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires List. Just days earlier, he had briefly climbed to No. 2 on that same list for the first time. Despite the sharp drop, there's little to suggest the sale is driven by financial necessity — Dell remains one of the wealthiest people in the world.Could buyers land a bargainThe auction is being handled by Paramount Realty USA in collaboration with SERHANT. Massachusetts. Paramount founder and CEO Misha Haghani acknowledged there's a real possibility a buyer could land a good deal, though he was careful to note that what counts as a "good deal" is ultimately subjective and will come down to how the market responds. Haghani declined to comment on why Dell is selling.Not Michael Dell's first headline-making property dealThis isn't Dell's first eye-catching real estate move. The Dell Technologies founder and CEO previously paid $100.47 million for a penthouse at Manhattan's One57 in 2014, a deal that set records at the time. His willingness to buy — and now sell — trophy properties at steep prices underscores a pattern of high-profile real estate bets that mirror the volatility of his tech fortune, which has swung dramatically in recent weeks alongside the broader AI-driven market turbulence hitting Dell Technologies stock.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: An 84-year-old Wyoming Navy veteran spent decades building a 207-acre llama ranch with his late wife; after donating it in 2025, the property has now opened as a sanctuary for veterans and first responders
articles.summary: US News: Al Ellis and his late wife Sondra had spent decades building the biggest vision of their lives, a 207-acre ranch near their two-story log home off US .
articles.body: Al Ellis and his late wife Sondra had spent decades building the biggest vision of their lives, a 207-acre ranch near their two-story log home off US Highway 191 in Boulder, a town of roughly 100 people 12 miles south of Pinedale. Ellis, an 84-year-old Navy veteran and former commercial driver, had turned to become a llama expert later in life.According to him, he has followed what he calls "butterfly moments", seemingly small encounters or decisions that, looking back, changed the direction of his life. On Friday, another such butterfly moment unfolded on his ranch. The land he once called a "hell hole" is now officially Boulder Crest Wyoming, a sanctuary where veterans, first responders and their families will have a place to step away from the weight of service, allowing them to reconnect and learn to grow in the aftermath of trauma.From 'hell hole' to homeEllis grew up in San Francisco where his parents ran a bodega and produce stand. “By the time you’re 8, you can take your orange crate down the street,” he said to Cowboy State Daily, remembering how children scavenged for things to put in discarded wooden crates.At 17, Ellis enlisted in the Navy, serving between the Korean and Vietnam wars. His time in the Navy eventually led him towards diving, which became the foundation for much of his adult life. He spent roughly two decades as a commercial fisherman and diver, harvesting abalone and sea urchins along the California coast. He also built businesses with Sondra, including seafood operations and restaurants.He bought a fishery with an old freezer that had, during World War II, stored shark livers for their vitamin A. He converted the fishery into a seafood restaurant named Andrea’s.Then the couple visited a friend in Alpine and fell in love with Wyoming. They eventually bought property near Jackson Hole, where Ellis began exploring the mountains.A llama sanctuarySoon, Ellis read an article about mountain pack llamas. He quickly acquired six llamas and spent the next decade guiding trips into the Wind River, Gros Ventre, Tetons and other nearby mountain ranges. “It was unbelievable how many people on my trips had never seen a night sky,” he said.As his herd grew, he realised that the 12-acre property wasn't enough. In 1998, the couple bought a run-down cattle ranch near Boulder. At the time, Ellis claims the property was an "eyesore." “I was enticing my wife from a 5,200-square-foot log home on the Snake River to come to a hell hole,” he said.But by 2012, they had transformed the property together, and it was home to about 200 llamas, including 60 pack llamas. The animals became Ellis' business, his passion and, eventually, the reason he and Sondra built the log home where they planned to grow old.Giving away his land for a causeThe idea of giving away his sprawling llama ranch began taking shape in the summer of 2025. Ellis was watching television when he came across Johnny "Joey" Jones, a military veteran and co-host of Fox News Channel's "The Big Weekend Show." Jones lost both legs to a roadside bomb in Iraq and wrote the New York Times bestseller, “Behind the Badge: Answering the Call to Serve on America’s Homefront.”Inspired, Ellis reached out to Jones by email and sought advice on how to go about gifting his property to serve veterans and his first responders. While he thought nothing would truly come out of the initiative, Jones saw his email and connected Ellis with Ken Falke, a retired Navy bomb disposal specialist and co-founder and chairman of the Boulder Crest Foundation.“As soon as I met (Ellis), it was like ‘wow,’” Falke told Cowboy State Daily. “I was a diver. He was a diver. I was in the Navy. He was in the Navy. There was this really interesting connection.” Within months, Ellis had entrusted Boulder Crest with the property.Sondra died in August 2025 after a lengthy health battle. The timing made the gift even more momentous. “Llamas are the reason this house is here,” Ellis said during Cowboy State Daily’s January visit. “We visualised being old here and wheeling over to the big windows to watch the llamas.” Now the house and land will have a different kind of life.Before Christmas 2025, Ellis donated the ranch along with the two-story log home to the Boulder Crest Foundation. His vision had always been for the land he and his wife built to continue to serve others. “We want other people to enjoy this space, people who deserve it, people who we owe something to,” Ellis told Cowboy State Daily in January.A space for the communityOn Friday, Boulder Crest formally introduced its Wyoming campus to community leaders, veterans, first responders and supporters from throughout the region in a grand opening. The celebration included a skydiving performance, the national anthem sung by local EMT and fourth-generation Sublette County rancher Sue Briggs-Stanfield, and a performance by the Wind River Indian Eagle Spirit Dancers. Ellis and his family were recognised throughout the program, as was another guest of honour, the land itself.Boulder Crest Foundation was founded with the idea that trauma does not have to be the end of the story. Its Posttraumatic Growth programs are designed to help veterans, first responders and their families move beyond simply coping with what happened to them and discover new strength, purpose and possibility. The PATHH program – Progressive and Alternative Training for Helping Heroes- helps veterans and first responders transform struggles into strength and thrive in the aftermath of trauma.The Wyoming campus will bring those programs to a region where geography itself can make accessing support difficult. “Al didn’t simply give us a piece of land, he entrusted us with the opportunity to create something that will serve people for generations,” Boulder Crest CEO Josh Goldberg said.Boulder Crest Wyoming will also host family rest and reconnection stays and couples programming. The campus is expected to be fully operational by September 2027. Boulder Crest said the location will serve not only Wyoming but the broader Mountain West as well.Moreover, the foundation will also include Ellis' llamas in its operations. “Watching baby llamas play when they’re in a group is 100% contagious,” Ellis said.The transformation of Ellis' property is already visible. Existing buildings have been renovated, said Boulder Crest Vice President of Communications Jennifer Grady, and much of the operational groundwork is complete.Kris Searles, Boulder Crest Wyoming's executive director, knows something about both the challenges of service and the character of the people who live in this part of the country. “My hope is that Boulder Crest Wyoming becomes a place our veterans, first responders, and families know belongs to them, but also a place this entire community feels connected to and proud of. We’re building something here that is rooted in Wyoming and designed to serve people for generations.”The regional mission is particularly important in a state where it is difficult to access specialised support. The latest U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs data shows Wyoming had a veteran suicide rate of 45.7 deaths per 100,000 veterans in 2023, higher than the national rate of 35.2.Boulder Crest Wyoming is the foundation's fourth campus, joining locations in Virginia, Arizona and Texas. The organisation says it reached more than 45,000 people through its programs in 2025 alone and has served more than 180,000 service members, veterans, first responders, military families, clinicians and helping professionals since 2014.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Rajarshi Mandal, the 16-year-old Lexington student whose malaria model showed the same mosquito-net supply could prevent twice as many infections; he won $50,000
articles.summary: US News: At 16, Rajarshi Mandal is already tackling a problem that has challenged public-health systems for decades: how to make limited malaria-prevention res.
articles.body: At 16, Rajarshi Mandal is already tackling a problem that has challenged public-health systems for decades: how to make limited malaria-prevention resources go further. The Lexington High School student built a mathematical model designed to determine where insecticide-treated mosquito nets could have the greatest impact, and his work earned him a $50,000 Davidson Fellows Scholarship, states an online report by the Davidson Institute. The report adds that Mandal, a rising junior from Lexington, Massachusetts, developed an ordinary differential equation model that simulates malaria transmission under conditions that more closely resemble the real world. His approach considers factors that standard population-based distribution can miss, including insecticide resistance, seasonal changes in transmission and the gradual deterioration of mosquito nets. Scroll down to read the details of his innovation.Rethinking where mosquito nets goInsecticide-treated nets are among the most affordable tools available for preventing malaria, but supplies are limited. According to the report, around 200 million nets are distributed globally each year, with allocations often based largely on population. Mandal wanted to know whether the same number of nets could prevent more infections if they were distributed differently. His simulation examined how malaria transmission changes across different settings and then evaluated where each available net could have the greatest effect. In his model, an optimized allocation prevented twice as many infections as a population-based approach using the same supply.Experts say that finding matters because it suggests that better allocation, rather than simply producing more nets, could potentially increase the impact of an existing public-health investment.From a newspaper image to a research projectFor Mandal, the idea began with footage showing fishermen using donated mosquito nets as fishing material because the mesh was available when conventional fishing equipment was not. The image prompted Mandal to look more closely at how mosquito nets are distributed and what happens when conditions on the ground do not match assumptions made in a distribution plan.His first attempt used a Deep Q Network, a type of machine-learning system. But the model struggled because allocation decisions produced noisy results and the benefits of those decisions could be delayed, making it difficult for the system to settle on reliable value estimates, states the report. Mandal eventually developed a different architecture that directly scored possible allocations, avoiding the instability he encountered with his original approach.Making the malaria model more realisticThe project also presented a problem that had little to do with machine learning. Early versions of Mandal's malaria simulation repeatedly drove infection levels down to zero, which did not reflect conditions in endemic regions.Guidance from researchers led him to investigate backward bifurcation, a phenomenon that can allow disease transmission to persist under circumstances where simpler models might predict elimination, explains the online report.He derived the model's reproduction number and confirmed that the simulation could sustain transmission at realistic mosquito-biting rates. The final framework incorporated seasonality, insecticide resistance, net degradation and the logistical challenges associated with reaching remote areas.Beyond the numbersMandal's interest in the project extends beyond improving a statistic. He points to the everyday consequences of malaria infections, including missed school, lost work and disruptions to farming and family responsibilities. The project also exposed him to the realities of delivering public-health interventions. A photograph of a transport truck overturned in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with mosquito nets scattered around it, underscored how easily logistical problems can interfere with even carefully designed programs, adds the report. For Mandal, the lesson is that mathematical modeling cannot eliminate every obstacle. It can, however, help make better decisions with the resources that reach their intended destinations.Alongside his research, Mandal studies advanced mathematics and computing, plays piano and has performed at Carnegie Hall twice. He also enjoys volleyball, skiing, mountain biking and karate, where he holds a black belt. The Davidson Fellows recognition places his malaria research among a broader community of young researchers, giving the 16-year-old both a scholarship and a larger platform for work aimed at turning better decisions into measurable health benefits.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Targets approved, bombs loaded & then Trump blinked: Why US pulled back from Houthi strikes
articles.summary: Middle East News: US President Donald Trump had moved to launch airstrikes against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) press.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump had moved to launch airstrikes against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) pressed him to intervene. But Trump abruptly halted the operation before the strikes could begin.A report by New York Times states that Trump had spent nearly two weeks wavering over whether to join Saudi Arabia in its renewed fight against the Houthis. On Wednesday, he told advisers he did not favour strikes. But after MBS called him on Thursday and again urged US military help, Trump reversed course and instructed the Pentagon to prepare airstrikes.According to two people briefed on the attack, Pentagon commanders had created approved target lists, troops were loading bombs onto warplanes selected for the missions and US military was prepared for fresh attacks on the Iranian proxy group. the wave of attacks was just about to begin.But by Sunday, however, Trump had reversed his decision yet again. The strikes were put on hold, at least for now, even as preparations for the attack had advanced significantly. The White House declined to discuss Trump's deliberations, while a senior administration official said only that the US had a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and would defend its allies.The sudden U-turn reflects a larger problem for Trump. The Houthis have avoided attacking US ships and have agreed, for now, not to fight the United States. But they have intensified attacks on Saudi Arabia, leaving Trump under pressure from a key ally that Washington also needs in its wider war against Iran.Saudi Arabia has shown it can use that dependence as leverage. In May, Riyadh effectively blocked a US plan to use American forces to escort commercial oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz by denying US forces access to its airspace and military bases.The Houthi threat has also expanded beyond Saudi Arabia. The group has attacked Saudi vessels and declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea, while capturing areas near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a crucial maritime chokepoint. The developments have raised fresh concerns over global shipping and energy supplies.Also read: Why Trump’s $24.3 billion Saudi F-35 deal is raising concerns in US, IsraelWhy is Trump hesitatingA new US bombing campaign would risk opening another front while American forces are already stretched by the war against Iran. Several officials and commanders have also questioned whether airstrikes would force the Houthis to back down.The US spent more than 50 days bombing the group in 2025, striking over 1,000 targets and burning through about $1 billion in weapons and ammunition in the first month. Trump later called a ceasefire, saying the Houthis had promised to stop attacking ships.The Houthis have since rebuilt much of their military capability and are now using artificial intelligence to develop and engineer new missile systems, according to US officials. A renewed US campaign could also prompt the group to resume attacks on American ships and further disrupt shipping through the Bab al-Mandab, adding another pressure point to already unstable energy routes.Trump said Sunday that he remained in “deciding mode” over the larger Iran war. For now, however, the president has stepped back from striking the Houthis, despite having taken the US military to the brink of doing so.Also read: 'Iran war has potential to escalate rapidly': US issues blanket Middle East travel alertCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Exercise Tarang Shakti is back': IAF announces resumption of multinational air exercise
articles.summary: News News: The Indian Air Force will host the second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti at Jodhpur in Rajasthan, bringing together air forces from multiple countr.
articles.body: The Indian Air Force will host the second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti at Jodhpur in Rajasthan, bringing together air forces from multiple countries for joint aerial operations, tactical training and interoperability drills. The exercise is expected to be held from September 26 to October 12.In a post on X, the Indian Air Force said, “Exercise Tarang Shakti is back,” describing the 2026 edition as India’s premier multinational air exercise and saying global air forces will come together for joint tactical manoeuvres.The upcoming exercise will be the second edition of Tarang Shakti, following the inaugural multinational air exercise held by the IAF in 2024. The 2026 edition is expected to provide participating air forces an opportunity to train together, exchange operational practices and conduct complex aerial missions.The exercise comes shortly after the India-Japan air combat exercise Veer Guardian 2026, which is being conducted at Jodhpur and is scheduled to conclude on September 22.Exercise Tarang Shakti is the Indian Air Force’s multinational air exercise, designed to bring together air forces from friendly countries for joint training, tactical coordination and interoperability. The first edition was held in 2024 and was conducted in two phases at Sulur in Tamil Nadu and Jodhpur in Rajasthan.The 2024 exercise involved air forces from several countries, including Australia, Bangladesh, France, Germany, Greece, Singapore, Spain, the UAE, the UK and the US. It featured fighter aircraft and other air assets operating alongside the IAF, allowing participating forces to practise complex aerial missions and exchange operational experience.The exercise is aimed at improving interoperability between participating air forces and providing them an opportunity to understand different operating procedures, tactics and mission-planning approaches. For the IAF, it also provides a platform to demonstrate and operate its indigenous and frontline aircraft alongside foreign platforms.

articles.title: In 1994, two friends set out to circle Earth without engines or sails; 13 years later, the journey ended after 46,505 miles and a crocodile attack
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 1994, Jason Lewis and Steve Smith set out to circle the Earth using human power rather than engines or sails. Thirteen years later, Lewis completed.
articles.body: In 1994, Jason Lewis and Steve Smith set out to circle the Earth using human power rather than engines or sails. Thirteen years later, Lewis completed the expedition after travelling 46,505 miles across five continents and numerous seas and oceans. In 2005, on the Cape York Peninsula in Australia, Lewis encountered a crocodile he estimated at 15 feet long. He knew estuarine crocodiles populated those waters. In his first-person account published by Sidetracked under the title “Crocodile Attack”, Lewis described how the crocodile followed his kayak to shore, attacked his paddle before retreating into deeper water. The encounter became one episode in his extraordinary 13-year circumnavigation.How did Jason Lewis survive the crocodile attackOne of the most dangerous episodes came on 13 May 2005 at Cape York Peninsula in Australia. Lewis recalled seeing two eyes and a snub nose gliding behind his kayak as he approached shore. He had already paddled twenty-two miles in five and a half hours, while a leak in the canvas hull had forced him to bail frequently. He described the experience as the “primal, fundamentally hard-wired horror of being hunted and considered prey”.Reaching the beach did not end the danger. Lewis wrote that the crocodile, which he estimated at 15 feet long, moved through the surf towards his kayak. Using the hull as protection, he prodded its snout with his paddle, but the animal opened its mouth, hissed and lunged at him. Its jaws caught the paddle blade, beginning a struggle in which Lewis eventually thrust the blade into its throat and struck at it, breaking the paddle. The crocodile then turned and slipped back into deeper water.Jason Lewis survived the night 25,000 miles from homeAfter the crocodile retreated, Lewis contacted John Andrews in Cairns using his satellite phone. Andrews warned him to leave the beach and seek higher ground, telling him that if he remained there overnight, the crocodile could wait until he was asleep. Lewis followed the advice and carried his equipment up the steep path to the top of the headland.By then it was dark. Lewis described his feet as swollen and said he was utterly spent as he sat in the windswept grass while mosquitoes gathered around him. Below, he could see the crocodile's eyes moving in the darkness. In his own account, he later reflected on how he had ended up “25,000 miles from home” on the cliff above a “man-eater”, after years of the expedition.Jason Lewis became the first to circle Earth by human powerThe Cape York encounter formed part of a much longer expedition that ultimately lasted 13 years. Lewis is recognised by Guinness World Records as the first person to circumnavigate the Earth without using motors or sails. Its account says he walked, cycled and inline skated across five continents and used kayaking, swimming, rowing and a pedal-powered boat to cross rivers, seas and oceans.According to Guinness World Records, Lewis completed the circumnavigation on 6 October 2007, having travelled 74,842 kilometres, or 46,505 miles. His route passed through antipodal points and covered more than the Earth's circumference of 24,900 miles, or 40,075 kilometres. The journey that began from Greenwich in 1994 therefore ended 13 years later with Lewis completing the first individual circumnavigation of the globe using human power.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Toledo woman's neighbour has a tree of heaven covered in spotted lanternflies, leaving her driveway, car and patio covered in bugs and sticky sap
articles.summary: US News: A Toledo woman says a spotted lanternfly infestation coming from a tree next door has gotten so bad that she can no longer park in her own driveway or.
articles.body: A Toledo woman says a spotted lanternfly infestation coming from a tree next door has gotten so bad that she can no longer park in her own driveway or use her backyard without dealing with the bugs and the mess they leave behind. Heather Keyes told 13 Action News she has tried almost everything to get rid of them, but the insects keep returning to the tree, a tree of heaven, that sits on the neighbouring property. After struggling to get help, she reached out to the station for support. Here's what she's dealing with, and how the property owner has responded so far.Heather Keyes says the infestation traces back to a neighbouring tree of heavenThe tree at the centre of the problem isn't Keyes' own; it sits in the yard next door, but the spotted lanternflies living around it, along with the sticky residue they leave behind, don't stay on that side of the property line. "I try to disturb their area, so maybe they'll go somewhere else, but they don't. They go right back to the tree," Keyes told 13 Action News. Her driveway sits just inches from the infested tree, which she said constantly drips sap onto everything nearby, effectively ruining anything she places outside.The mess spreading onto Keyes' driveway, patio and carKeyes said the tree has made basic use of her own property nearly impossible. "I can't park my car back here, I can't even sit back here. It's just so gross with everything. Not just the bugs, but the tree just drips constantly," she told 13 Action News. She said her car, trash cans and patio furniture have all been coated in sap from the tree, adding that whatever she puts outside, she has to accept it will likely get ruined by the ongoing mess.How long the lanternfly problem has been building next doorKeyes has lived at her home for seven years, and said the neighbouring tree was the size of a weed when she first moved in. The lanternflies became a noticeable problem about a year ago, and Keyes said she has since killed hundreds of them trying to keep the infestation under control. Her landlord has trimmed back what growth they can reach from her side of the property line, but the core of the problem remains rooted in the neighbouring tree itself, which continues to host the insects.The property owner's response to Keyes' concernsAccording to county records, the neighbouring property has been owned by Mercer Holdings 1 LLC since February, with a related business, Mercer Maintenance LLC, sharing the same address; both trace back to an address on Upton Avenue. Mercer Maintenance's website advertises tree trimming among its services for rental properties. The maintenance director of the company confirmed he was aware of the property and the tree issue, and said he had spoken with Keyes before, telling the station that Keyes is able to trim the portion of the tree extending onto her own property.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
