articles.title: In 1959, Sebastian Scirpo started a Connecticut livestock auction in a rented chicken coop and made $7 on his first commission; 67 years later, his daughters run the state's last remaining sale barn
articles.summary: US News: Since her father died in 2002, Lisa Scirpo has been working to persuade farmers and dealers that the Middlesex Livestock Auction will continue as the .
articles.body: Since her father died in 2002, Lisa Scirpo has been working to persuade farmers and dealers that the Middlesex Livestock Auction will continue as the only sale barn in Connecticut. Without it, Scirpo said farmers who want to bring animals to auction would have to travel to Massachusetts or Pennsylvania. But now, farmers in those states come to Middlefield.Scirpo had grown up on the farm watching the animals and the buyers go buy and her father helmed the process. After his death, she went farm to farm with notices, telling people that she could take over. While she initially faced scepticism from farmers, over the past few decades she has proved that she can keep Middlesex Livestock Auction going.Her father, Sebastian Scirpo built much of the place as it is today. The old bleachers, the sale ring where the animals are presented, the chute they go through after the sale and the scale on which they are weighed. “Every cement block you see here, my father built,” she said to CT Insider.A father's dreamSebastian started the auction in 1959. He began in a rented chicken coop on Little Lane and made $7 on his first commission. He had grown up near his grandmother's farm and loved animals, said his daughter. He also worked in auto body and could fix almost anything. But he wanted a sale barn, so he converted the chicken coop and kept going.In 1970, the family bought the Cherry Hill Road property. Scirpo said her father and relatives built the auction by hand, brick by brick. He did not teach his daughters that livestock were just products moving through a market. “He always taught us that the animals came first because they couldn’t help themselves,” she said. “They needed to be taken care of.”The family has maintained the auction through the ups and downs. When Scirpo was a child, her father lost his feet in a corn chopper. Doctors talked about amputating his legs but another doctor asked if he could try to sew them back together. Sebastian survived and went from moving around in a wheelchair to using a walker, crutches and a cane. He later wore special shoes and learned to walk again. Decades later, Scirpo ran into one of the men who had been there that day. He told her that her father, trapped and in agony, had asked him to shoot him. It was the first time she had heard that part of the story.Sebastian Scirpo lived more than 30 years after the accident, dying at age 66, after becoming ill at the auction. The family later faced another farm accident. Scirpo said her sister, Lana, slipped off a Super M tractor and got her arm caught in the power takeoff. It happened on Feb. 11, their father’s birthday.Lana survived, but lost her arm. She now runs the auction with her sister. Then there was cancer. Lisa Scirpo said she was diagnosed about six years ago. Even while getting radiation, she said, she still came to the auction on Mondays.Scirpo understands that when people hear "livestock auction", they think of slaughterhouses, meat prices and animals being treated like commodities. While she does not pretend that animals sold at the auction are not part of that system, she stands firm with the idea that the people running the barn are careful with them. Years ago, she said, protesters came to the property. She did not throw them off. She brought them water.“I understand,” she said. “But we don’t allow brutality to animals.”Keeping it all aliveWhen Sebastian died, his wife Kathleen and daughter Lisa took over the work. They built back the business and kept it alive. Until recently, the auction's paperwork was done by hand. Kathleen printed checks by hand, wrote out envelopes and handled money. Lisa's aunt Barbara also helped.But a few years ago, Lisa finally incorporated computers to make it easier for her mother and aunt. The day after they were installed, her mother was supposed to come in and learn how things would work. Instead, her aunt found she had peacefully died in her sleep.In 1970, the auction was one among many in Connecticut, but now, it's the only one left. The state had 5,058 farms in the 2022 Census of Agriculture, down from the previous census, with 372,000 acres of farmland and $704 million in agricultural production. The number of Connecticut farms with cattle and calves fell from 1,158 in 2017 to 876 in 2022, according to U.S. Department of Agriculture data.State Agriculture Commissioner Bryan P. Hurlburt said Connecticut has invested in animal health, biosecurity, food systems that prioritise buying from Connecticut farms and grants for livestock producers, as well as expanded local processing capacity. “These coordinated initiatives reflect our commitment to building a robust, adaptable agricultural landscape that enhances the state’s overall food security,” Hurlburt said.The state Department of Agriculture posts Middlesex Livestock Auction prices online, with categories for calves, cattle, sheep, goats, rabbits, poultry and other animals. Scirpo said that public market matters because it gives farmers another option.The farmers don't have to use the auction and they can sell directly to a dealer. But then, they may be sacrificing the best price. An auction, Scirpo said is a gamble. Prices move, buyers change and markets rise and fall. Here, farmers can see what their animals are worth in public.A family operationToday, the auction is still run by the family. Scirpo is 62; her sister Lana is 67. Their aunt Barbara is 83, and all of them still work in the office. On sale days, cattle sales begin at 6 p.m., Lisa Scirpo said. Some Mondays, they do not leave until 1 a.m. Then she still has horses at home to care for. Her father had a saying: "There is plenty of sleep when you’re dead." “That’s the way we were brought up,” she said.The work is part livestock, part paperwork, part crowd control, part market analysis and part endurance test. The auction has licenses for different parts of the business. The animals move through the chute and onto the scale. The auctioneer keeps the sale moving.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: PATNA: Jamui Police has launched an investigation after two videos allegedly showing the harassment of a Class 10 girl by a group of youths surfaced on social media. The videos purportedly show the girl being stopped on the road, subjected to inappropriate physical contact and allegedly dragged by some of the youths.Police have identified the minor victims and registered an FIR after taking cognisance of the viral footage.According to preliminary information, the incident occurred on the evening of September 19 in the Sadar police station area of Jamui. The girl and a Class 10 boy, both minors and residents of Jamui town, had reportedly gone to Marwa Pahad on a scooter after attending coaching classes.Read more: 'Hands, legs tied': Delhi girl 'sexually assaulted' inside shop after being luredWhile returning, a group of youths allegedly stopped them on the road. During the incident, the youths allegedly behaved inappropriately with the girl, while another person recorded portions of the episode.In one of the videos, several youths can be seen surrounding the girl and questioning her about her name and residence. The boy accompanying her is allegedly separated from her, while the girl remains surrounded by the group.The footage purportedly shows some youths engaging in inappropriate physical contact with the girl and dragging her on the road. At one point, some people appear to intervene and try to rescue her. However, other youths allegedly approach again and the harassment continues.Read more: Jaipur hit-and-run: 57-year-old dies after speeding Thar hits scooter, CCTV emergesThe incident is believed to have continued for around 20 minutes, although two videos of approximately 1 minute 2 seconds and 35 seconds have surfaced. A second video allegedly shows the girl being stopped again before some youths allow her to leave.Initially, the victims and their families did not approach the police. However, after the videos surfaced on social media, Jamui Police took cognisance of the matter, traced the victims and began an investigation.Jamui SP Vishwajit Dayal said, “A case had been registered at Nagar police station in connection with the viral videos and the alleged harassment of the minor boy and girl.”The SP said the incident occurred on September 19 and that the police had not received information from the victims or their families immediately after the incident. The investigation was initiated after the videos went viral, following which police contacted the victim.According to the SP, “No accused was named in the FIR. Investigators are identifying those involved on the basis of the videos and other evidence. The role of other suspects will be examined after the alleged main accused is identified and arrested.”The police are also verifying the authenticity and location of the videos and examining the circumstances in which they were recorded.Investigators are questioning people connected with the incident and collecting other available evidence.The SP described the incident as unfortunate and said strict action would be taken against all those found involved on the basis of evidence.He also said that since the case involved minors, the families had not immediately approached the police.Police said the investigation is continuing and further action will follow as the identities and individual roles of the accused are established.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: “It takes a lot of mental strength,”  IIT Kanpur graduate left her corporate job and start up to travel, but what she learnt in these six years was an eye-opener and an ultimate lesson
articles.summary: For years, Kanak Agrawal’s life seemed to be following a familiar definition of success. She studied at IIT Kanpur, landed a job with McKinsey in Gurg.
articles.body: For years, Kanak Agrawal’s life seemed to be following a familiar definition of success. She studied at IIT Kanpur, landed a job with McKinsey in Gurgaon and later co-founded a startup, spending five years building it.On paper, it was the kind of career trajectory many young professionals work towards. But somewhere along the way, Kanak realised that the life she was building did not quite feel like her own. “I didn’t quit because any of it was bad. I quit because none of it felt mine,” she says.That decision eventually took her in a very different direction- away from corporate offices and conventional career milestones and towards a life built around travel, writing, content creation and the freedom to decide how she spends her days.From IIT Kanpur to McKinsey and a startupAgrawal grew up near Kota, where IIT coaching was a major part of the environment around her. Her brother had gone to IIT, and she followed a similar path, eventually joining IIT Kanpur.Even her entry into the corporate world followed a familiar pattern. McKinsey selected her, and she joined the consulting firm in Gurgaon. But less than two years into the job, she left.Her next chapter was a startup. Friends were working on an idea and she joined them, eventually becoming a co-founder and spending about five years with the company.The startup experience was valuable, but it did not resolve the larger question she had been carrying. “Things went well, but I didn’t feel satisfied,” she told Moneycontrol. At 31, Agrawal decided to walk away again.This time, there was no obvious next corporate role waiting for her.When work stopped deciding what her life looked likeThe biggest change was not simply where Agrawal worked, but how she experienced an ordinary day. At McKinsey, she remembered mornings as rushed and anxious. During her startup years, there was always something pending or something that needed fixing. Her days revolved around work and its demands.Life now looks very different. Living amid the hills in Himachal Pradesh, Agrawal says that her mornings can begin quietly, with hot water and 30-40 minutes of journalling. She cooks for herself, has fewer meetings and makes room for people, hobbies and rest. “I don’t have to wait for permission to live,” she said.Her income, however, has also changed. Agrawal works as a content creator and ghostwriter, takes up selected brand collaborations and hosts slow-living experiences for small groups. She has travelled slowly across India and abroad, often living out of a backpack.She openly acknowledges that she earns less than she once did. “Mostly, I’m happy because this life feels like mine,” she said, while also admitting that she sometimes thinks about the opportunity cost of choosing a different path.The loneliness that comes with freedomThe decision has not made every part of life easier. In a recent reflection, Agrawal wrote about reconnecting with an old friend after 12 years. During their conversation, she spoke about her life on the road and also admitted that she sometimes feels lonely because she is not physically close to her friends.Her friend asked her a pointed question: if she was earning only a fraction of what some of her IIT peers were earning and did not have a fixed social circle, what had this life actually given her?Agrawal said it was a fair question. Her answer was not about money or career achievements. After years of travelling, she said, unfamiliar places no longer frighten her in the same way. She has repeatedly experienced strangers helping her- offering food, shelter, rides or changing their own plans to ensure she reaches somewhere safely.Those encounters, she says, gradually changed her relationship with the world.Learning to trust strangersOne of the less obvious things Agrawal says she gained from travelling was trust.She recalled that she has never carried pepper spray or another self-defence tool, saying she never felt the need to. For her, the repeated experience of strangers being kind created a different kind of confidence: the belief that even when she does not know what to do next, she will probably figure it out- and if she cannot, somebody may help.That is perhaps the biggest shift in her journey. Travel did not simply take her from one destination to another; it changed how she viewed uncertainty.Instead of trying to control every outcome, she learnt to believe that she could navigate what came next.What she gave up- and what she got backAgrawal does not pretend that her choice came without costs. She earns less than many of her IIT peers. She does not have a fixed group of friends she can meet every weekend. Her life lacks the predictability of a conventional career and a permanent home.Her parents, too, were initially shocked when she quit McKinsey and later the startup. Even now, she says, they would prefer that she had stayed on the corporate path and settled in one place. But they have allowed her to make her own choices.There are still moments when she compares herself with people from her peer group. But she also hears from some of them that they envy the flexibility she has created for herself.The harder challenge, she says, is sustaining this kind of life without losing financial stability or authenticity. Working for yourself means there is no boss setting the structure and no conventional safety net.“It takes a lot of mental strength,” she said. Yet that uncertainty is precisely what makes the journey meaningful to her.After years of moving from place to place, Agrawal says she can arrive somewhere she knows nobody and still feel at home. The life is not perfectly sorted, nor is it presented as a blueprint for everyone. It is simply a life she chose after spending years following paths that seemed right on paper.And perhaps that is what has changed most: success, for Agrawal, is no longer only about how much she earns or how impressive her résumé looks. It is about waking up and knowing that the life in front of her is one she deliberately chose.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: 'We'll change geography of war': Iran warns US of new weapons, targets
articles.summary: Middle East News: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Monday warned that any fresh escalation with the United States could see Tehran deploy new weapons,.
articles.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Monday warned that any fresh escalation with the United States could see Tehran deploy new weapons, adopt new military tactics and target locations that have not previously been struck.IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Iran was prepared for a prolonged confrontation and that there would be “significant changes” in its defensive and counteroffensive operations if hostilities intensified.“Those changes include a shift in the geography of war, and a shift in weapons and military equipment,” he told local media. “We will bring new weapons with new capabilities into the battlefield, and the world will be astonished.”Mohebbi also warned that Iran's targets would not necessarily be the same as those targeted during the earlier phase of the conflict.“Our targets are also no longer necessarily the same [as the] previous targets. We have new targets that have not yet been struck,” he said.In an interview with Al-Alam News Network, Mohebbi said the IRGC had prepared for a “long-term war” and would respond if the conflict entered another phase of heightened hostilities.“In our view, war is war; it has different stages, but war is war and the war is not over, the war continues, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has prepared itself for a long-term war, and it was ready before, and now it is even more prepared for a long-term war,” he said.Mohebbi also claimed that the United States, Israel and their allies had failed to achieve their objectives in the conflict. He specifically pointed to the Strait of Hormuz, saying the US had failed to reopen the strategic waterway despite deploying its military capabilities to the region.“Despite America having the largest navy in the world and despite defining the reason for its presence in the region and the world as ensuring the security of energy flows and freedom of navigation, it became clear in this war that America, first of all, did not have the ability to reopen the Strait and could not,” he said.The remarks come amid continuing tensions in West Asia following the US-Israel attacks on Iran on February 28 and Iran's subsequent retaliatory operations.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: BMW that plunged off Mumbai's Coastal Road bridge had earlier hit couple, video viral
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A speeding BMW that crashed through a barrier on Mumbai’s Coastal Road and plunged off a bridge, killing three students on Sunday, was involve.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A speeding BMW that crashed through a barrier on Mumbai’s Coastal Road and plunged off a bridge, killing three students on Sunday, was involved in a separate incident and had an FIR lodged at Gamdevi police station in March this year for overspeeding. A video of the six-month-old incident has now surfaced on social media.Omkar Shirke, who filed the complaint, was travelling with his wife when the BMW hit them on March 29. Shirke had also recorded a video of the incident at the time. The footage, now circulating widely on social media, shows Shirke and a man driving the BMW during the March incident.The complaint had been filed before Sunday’s accident, in which three occupants of the BMW were killed and another was critically injured after the high-end car plunged from Mumbai’s Coastal Road.At least six people have died in accidents on the Coastal Road since it opened in March 2024. The toll rises to seven if the connected BKC stretch is included.Fatal Coastal Road crash: Three students killed, one injuredThree students, including a minor, were killed and another was injured after the BMW crashed through a Coastal Road barrier at high speed and fell about 75 metres into an under-construction site near Lotus Jetty in Worli around 5.20am on Sunday. CCTV footage showed the car speeding before plunging from the second-level ramp, a height of about 70ft, while heading towards Haji Ali from Marine Drive.Police said the driver appeared to have lost control while speeding. The deceased were identified as Dhairya Sheth, 17, Aditya Jakasania, 19, and Shanay Gajjar, 21, who was driving his family car. Aditya Oswal, 23, suffered multiple injuries and is being treated at BYL Nair Hospital. All four were from Gujarat and were studying at two colleges in Mumbai.The crash came to light after a motorist alerted the police control room that a vehicle had fallen from the road. A police team reached the area and, while trying to locate the exact spot, was directed there by a watchman who had witnessed the accident. The four occupants were taken by ambulance to Nair Hospital, where doctors declared three of them dead.CCTV footage showed the BMW speeding before the crash. The impact was severe: one victim was thrown about 20ft from the car, while another was found outside the vehicle. Police said Gajjar, who was driving, was still partly inside the car, with his leg on the accelerator. All airbags had deployed.Police traced the BMW through its registration number and contacted Gajjar’s father, who arrived in Mumbai to claim his son’s body.Gajjar and Oswal were studying architecture at a college in Kurla, while Sheth and Jakasania were students at a well-known management college in the western suburbs. The four were staying in hostels or as paying guests in Santacruz and Juhu.Senior inspector Mina Jagtap of Tardeo police said blood samples of the victims had been collected and would be sent to the Kalina Forensic Science Laboratory. The postmortems were conducted at Nair Hospital.Police said they would register accidental death cases and also cases under relevant provisions for causing death by negligence and rash and negligent driving. Police did not confirm reports that one of the victims was wearing a party ribbon. Families in AhmedabadIn Ahmedabad, a pall of gloom descended on the homes of Gajjar and Jakasania after news of their deaths reached their families.At Gajjar’s home in Swastik Society, Navrangpura, relatives gathered as his parents left for Mumbai.“Everybody here is in a state of shock. We are still processing the events,” a relative said.Jakasania’s family had also left their home at Shompole Apartment near Sindhu Bhavan for Mumbai. articles.summary: Middle East News: Dubai has declared 10 days of official mourning following the death of Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, younger brother of Dubai’s Ruler Sheikh Moh.
articles.body: Dubai has declared 10 days of official mourning following the death of Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, younger brother of Dubai’s Ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.According to Gulf News, Sheikh Ahmed, Deputy Chairman of Dubai Police and Public Security, died on Monday, September 21.The Ruler’s Court announced that the mourning period would begin immediately, with flags to be flown at half-mast across the emirate.Sheikh Mohammed, who is also the UAE’s Vice President and Prime Minister, paid tribute to his younger brother in a post on X, praying for his mercy and a place in Paradise.“May Allah have mercy on Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum. May Allah have mercy on you, my brother,” Sheikh Mohammed wrote. He added that although Ahmed was no longer with them, he would remain in their prayers and hearts.Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, also mourned his uncle and prayed for his forgiveness and mercy.Born in 1950, Sheikh Ahmed was the youngest son of the late Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum, former Ruler of Dubai. He graduated from the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst and later joined Dubai’s Central Military Command, eventually becoming its Commander-in-Chief.He also served as Deputy Chairman of Dubai Police and Public Security and held senior positions linked to Dubai’s security establishment. He was also associated with business, real estate and sports interests in the emirate, including A.R.M. Holding and Dubai Real Estate Centre.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Non-application of mind': Court sets aside order refusing probe in Sonia Gandhi electoral roll case
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday allowed a revision plea challenging a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Soni.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday allowed a revision plea challenging a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral roll in 1980, three years before she acquired Indian citizenship.Special Judge Vishal Gogne delivered the judgment two days after deferring it. He quashed the order as "non-speaking" or an order that does not explain the reasons behind a judge's conclusion."The impugned order suffers from a manifest error in law on account of non-compliance with Section 175(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), inter alia, not hearing the submissions of the police officer concerned and non-calling of a status report from the police station concerned," the Special Judge noted."The 'non-speaking' nature of the order was evident as the magistrate did not consider the twin options under law of directing the registration of an FIR or alternatively conducting proceedings under the BNSS, and instead of considering the core aspect of whether the complaint disclosed the commission of a cognisable offence, the magistrate digressed towards the issue of citizenship," he added.The court remanded the matter back to the magistrate to pass a reasoned order after hearing fresh arguments.The matter has been posted for further proceedings on September 29.In September last year, advocate Vikas Tripathi filed a plea in a Delhi magistrate's court seeking action against Sonia Gandhi, claiming her name appeared on the electoral rolls three years before she became an Indian citizen in 1983. The plea had sought a police investigation into what it terms a possible case of forgery.The application had pointed to documents suggesting Sonia Gandhi took Indian citizenship on April 30, 1983. Yet, her name allegedly appeared as a voter in the New Delhi constituency roll in 1980, was deleted in 1982, and re-entered in April 1983 after she formally became an Indian national.Tripathi's plea was dismissed on September 11, 2025, prompting him to approach a higher court.(With PTI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Middle East News: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said the conflict with the United States and its allies is 'not over', warning that Tehran is prep.
articles.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said the conflict with the United States and its allies is 'not over', warning that Tehran is prepared for a prolonged confrontation if hostilities intensify in West Asia.In an interview with Al-Alam News Network, IRGC second brigadier general Hossein Mohebbi said Iranian forces had prepared for a "long-term war" and remained ready to respond to any fresh escalation."In our view, war is war; it has different stages, but war is war and the war is not over, the war continues, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has prepared itself for a long-term war, and it was ready before, and now it is even more prepared for a long-term war," Mohebbi said, according to news agency ANI.He added that any renewed escalation would trigger an Iranian response."And this is not a new stage, so to speak, but if at another stage we encounter the issue of the intensity of our aggression again, without a doubt we are prepared and we will defend ourselves," he said.Mohebbi also claimed that the United States, Israel and their allies had failed to achieve their objectives during the conflict."America has failed in this war, and its defeat is a historic and shameful defeat, but it does not have the courage to admit this defeat and accept it," he said, adding that the assessment was shared by military and political experts.A key part of his remarks concerned the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has sought to control amid the wider conflict."One of the areas of America's failure is the failure to reopen the Strait of Hormuz," Mohebbi said, claiming that the US "did not have the ability to reopen the Strait and could not".Separately, according to Fars News, Mohebbi warned that any fresh US offensive would lead Iran to alter both its weapons and the locations targeted."If a new aggression occurs, we will certainly change the weaponry and the geography of the war," he said, reiterating that Tehran was prepared for a prolonged conflict.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Railways ordered to pay Rs 35,000 to passenger as train delayed by more than 8 hours
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Jharkhand has the Railways to pay Rs 30,000 compensation to a passenger who faced a 8 hours and 48 minute.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Jharkhand has the Railways to pay Rs 30,000 compensation to a passenger who faced a 8 hours and 48 minutes delay while travelling from Tatanagar to Sambalpur. The commission also awarded Rs 5,000 as litigation costs, holding that the Railways failed to show that the delay was beyond its control. The order was passed on September 2, 2026.Why did the passenger approach the consumer commission?According to the commission order, Sanjay Kumar had booked two sleeper-class tickets on the Ispat Express for travel from Tatanagar to Sambalpur on September 23, 2024. The train was scheduled to leave Tatanagar at 10.18 am and reach Sambalpur at 3.50 pm.The train departed late and reached Sambalpur 528 minutes (8 hours and 48 minutes) behind schedule. Kumar claimed Rs 4.5 lakh compensation for the physical, mental and financial harassment he said he suffered because of the delay. He submitted his ticket and a legal notice sent to the Railways in support of his complaint.However, the Railways denied the complaint and questioned the commission's jurisdiction, saying the matter came under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act. It also argued that IRCTC and Kharagpur division had not been made parties to the case.The Railways further said Kumar had not complied with the required notice provision and had not produced substantive evidence of financial loss or damage caused by the delay. It denied any deficiency in service.Why did the commission hold the Railways liable?The bench of President Sunil Kumar Singh and members Pradeep Kumar Mishra and Sanju Shahi first dealt with the objection over its jurisdiction. It referred to a Supreme Court ruling concerning compensation for train delays and said the consumer commission could hear Kumar's complaint.The commission noted that the Railways had not shown that the delay was beyond its control.“So Honble S.C has categorically held that this commission has got Jurisdiction to try the instant case. In this case O.P’s failed to establish that the delay of train occurred which was beyond their control. So we find much substance in claim of the complainant against the O.P’s,” the bench observed.The commission then considered whether Kumar had proved that he suffered because of the delay. It relied on his ticket and other documents placed on record.“So in view of discussion made above we are of considered view that the complainant has proved his case by cogent and convincing evidence that due to late running of train by O.P’s complainant suffered physical mental and financial harassment and accordingly complainant is entitled to compensation from the O.P’s for their deficiency in service,” the commission further added.The commission also relied on the Supreme Court's observation that passengers' time is valuable and that the Railways must explain delays and show when they were beyond its control.“It cannot be disputed that every passengers time is precious unless and until the evidence is laid explaining the delay and it is established and proved that delay occurred which was beyond their control and even there was some Justification for delay,” the Supreme Court passage cited in the order said.The commission partly allowed Kumar's complaint and directed the opposite parties to pay Rs 30,000 as compensation for harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.The amount was to be paid within 45 days from the date of the order. If it was not paid within that period, the commission directed that the amount would carry interest at 12 percent per annum from the date of the order until realisation.

articles.title: Rick Ross bought Evander Holyfield’s 235-acre Georgia estate for $5.8 million in 2014, added 87 acres for $1 million and turned the roughly 322-acre property into his Promise Land ranch
articles.summary: US News: Rapper Rick Ross bought former heavyweight boxing champion Evander Holyfield’s Georgia estate for $5.8 million in 2014. The property, near Fayettevill.
articles.body: Rapper Rick Ross bought former heavyweight boxing champion Evander Holyfield’s Georgia estate for $5.8 million in 2014. The property, near Fayetteville, had a 45,000-square-foot mansion with 109 rooms, 12 bedrooms and 21 bathrooms, according to Architectural Digest. Ross later expanded the estate by buying another 87 acres for $1 million.The estate, once known as Villa Vittoriosa, became Ross’s Promise Land. The rapper had been familiar with the property for years before he bought it. He had purchased a nearby house after moving to Georgia and said he used to drive past Holyfield’s home regularly.“I looked at every curve and every up and downhill on the lawn. I was looking at the geese as I rolled by. I did that for years until one day, I saw the red for-sale sign on the gate and made a U-turn,” Ross told Forbes in a 2021 interview.Ross’s interest in property was also influenced by his mother. He said she believed real estate was an important way to protect and grow his money. In the same interview, Ross recalled her advice- “She would just keep buying houses,” he said, adding, "when you buy something, make sure you can touch it.” Over the years, Ross went on to build a property portfolio across Georgia, Florida and Texas.The Georgia estate remained one of the most notable properties in that portfolio. After buying Holyfield’s former home, Ross added 87 adjoining acres in 2019. The expanded property covered roughly 322 acres. He also began using the estate for large gatherings, including a car show and pool party that were open to the public during the summer.A 109-room mansion with a huge poolThe mansion was originally built in 1994 and covers about 45,000 square feet. Its 109 rooms include 12 bedrooms and 21 bathrooms. The dining room is large enough to seat 100 people, while the property also has a 350,000-gallon swimming pool.The property was used as the fictional Zamunda Palace in the 2021 film Coming 2 America, starring Eddie Murphy. The mansion's white stone exterior and large entrance helped it fit the look required for the film.For Ross, however, the estate has also been a personal project. He has spoken about spending time looking after the land and even mowing parts of it himself. For this, he also bought a tractor with an enclosed cabin, air conditioning and a radio.“I bought a tractor that is enclosed and has air-conditioning and a radio. When I get in the tractor, it’s a whole other level of peace and a whole other level of connecting with the estate and the animals and the birds and the wildlife,” he said.Ross also keeps animals on the property. He reportedly owns two buffaloes, four horses and a bull. The buffaloes have also led to complaints from neighbours.The Georgia property was not the only major estate Ross bought as his music career grew. His approach to real estate continued with purchases in Florida and later Texas.Florida estate for $3.5 millionIn 2021, Ross bought a 2.3-acre estate in Southwest Ranches, Florida, for $3.5 million in cash. His mother and sister had been helping him look for a property in the Miami Beach area when they came across the home.The property had previously belonged to Ross’s friend and NBA All-Star Amar’e Stoudemire, who had owned the single-storey residence for about a decade. Ross said he knew quickly that he wanted the house after seeing it. “This is my house,” he told his agent after seeing the property.The 8,600-square-foot home has six bedrooms and seven bathrooms. It also includes high ceilings, two home offices, an indoor theatre, a gym and a swimming pool with a waterfall.Houston and Atlanta purchases In early 2023, Ross revealed another property purchase in Houston. He shared pictures of the home on Instagram and referred to himself as “Rodeo Rick”.He later showed parts of the property in a video tour. “While others was buying Dogecoin and all that, man, I was buying real estate,” Ross said in the video.He showed the home's pool, front gate and palm trees, saying some of the trees had been brought from Miami. The video also showed white walls and artwork.About a week after the Houston purchase was reported, Ross bought another Atlanta-area property. He paid $4.2 million in cash to fellow rapper and friend Meek Mill for the estate.The three-storey house has eight bedrooms and nine-and-a-half bathrooms. It also includes a tennis court, media room, two-car garage, sauna and pool. Ross bought the property unfurnished.$37 million Star Island homeRoss's property purchases in 2023 also included a much larger deal in Miami. A few months after the Houston and Atlanta purchases, he paid $37 million for a waterfront home on guard-gated Star Island.The community has 30 residences. Ross's property covers 12,374 square feet and has six bedrooms and eight-and-a-half bathrooms. The house includes a primary suite facing the bay and outdoor areas designed for gatherings. It also has a 40-foot dock that provides access to the bay and the ocean beyond.ONE Sotheby's International Realty global real estate adviser Kimberly Knausz told Architectural Digest that Ross viewed the Star Island purchase as an important part of his property portfolio.“Star Island is the ultimate goal in Miami. It’s so exclusive, Ross said it’s like the missing piece to the puzzle of his real estate portfolio,” Knausz said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A Wisconsin family had farmed the same West Bend land since 1847 and George Muth became its fifth generation farmer; 179 years later, bulldozers have demolished the old barn for a new housing development
articles.summary: US News: A Wisconsin family had farmed the same land in West Bend since 1847, with George Muth becoming the fifth generation of his family to work the farm. On.
articles.body: A Wisconsin family had farmed the same land in West Bend since 1847, with George Muth becoming the fifth generation of his family to work the farm. On Friday, the old barn on the Muth family property was demolished as the land is being cleared for a new housing development.According to Washington County Insider, bulldozers pushed the remains of the barn past its fieldstone foundation while trees in a nearby field were also cut down. The new development is planned to include about 400 multifamily residences.The property is located at the northwest corner of Paradise Drive and River Road. George Muth recalled how the area looked when he was growing up and farming there."That was always farm field," George said. "It was corn, soybeans and hay and I farmed it when I was young and I was fifth generation to farm it," he said.George also remembered a time when all four corners around the area were farmland. Paradise Drive, he said, was once "a very skinny, one-lane road." The area has since changed, with the family property now being cleared for a residential development.A family farm since 1847The Muth family's connection with the property goes back nearly 180 years. George's memories of the property are tied to a time when the surrounding area was largely made up of farm fields. The demolition of the barn came as the property was being prepared for the new subdivision.The change has also raised concerns among some neighbours living near Paradise Drive and River Road. Neighbours have expressed concerns about the new development and safety related to additional traffic on River Road.The Muth family had also been known in the area for another business across the road, Egbert & Guido's Express Inc. George and Kathy Muth owned the business, which operated as a Citgo gas station before it was sold to Kwik Trip.Family sold gas station after 21 yearsThe Muths had operated the gas station for 21 years before selling it to Kwik Trip in 2018. Washington County Insider reported back then that the sale had been confirmed.Kathy Muth spoke about the reaction from customers and the difficulty of closing the business after more than two decades."We've had a couple tearful days this week along with a lot of our loyal customers who were sad to see us closing the store," Kathy said. "It wasn't an easy decision but it made sense."The business was named Egbert & Guido's after George's father, Egbert, and his uncle, Guido.At the time of the sale, George said the family was not retiring. He explained that the gas station was being sold as a business decision, while the family still had a dairy farm in Fillmore."We are not retiring," George said. "It's just a business we're selling. We still have the dairy farm in Fillmore. The gas station was something my wife ran."The old gas station site also carried a farewell message after the sale. A sign near the corner of Paradise Drive read, "Thanks for 21 years. Bon voyage." George said the message was the employees' idea.Another sign on the door thanked customers and staff for 21 years at the business and expressed the family's gratitude for their support.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bihar harassment case: NCW takes suo motu cognizance, demands immediate arrest of perpetrators
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Women (NCW) on Monday took suo motu cognizance of harassment and assault of a young woman and her male companio.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Women (NCW) on Monday took suo motu cognizance of harassment and assault of a young woman and her male companion in Bihar’s Jamui district, after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.NCW chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to Bihar director general of police, calling for the immediate registration of an FIR, identification and arrest of all those involved, and a time-bound and impartial investigation.The commission has specifically asked authorities to use the video footage to identify the alleged perpetrators and take action against them.The incident reportedly took place on the evening of September 19. Bihar Police said the woman and the man were allegedly stopped and harassed by a group of people by the roadside.Jamui Police said that an FIR had been registered and SIT was formed to probe the incident. Moreover, 3 people have been taken into custody."An FIR has been registered regarding the incident of molestation and indecent behavior by anti-social elements shown in the video, and a SIT has been constituted under the leadership of the Sub-Divisional Police Officer of Jamui; the team is conducting continuous raids. Based on identifications made from the video, three individuals have been taken into custody," news agency ANI quoted SP Vishwajeet Dayal saying."Two others have been identified, and efforts are underway to arrest them as well... As for the main accused—the one who appears to have behaved indecently with the woman—he has been identified, and we are making efforts to arrest him soon; we are actively working on this... We will take action against those attempting to tarnish the reputation of Jamui district... We have arrested three minors so far; as the investigation proceeds and more individuals are taken into custody...," he added.According to the SP, the young man and woman are friends and attend the same coaching institute. He did not disclose additional details, saying, “We must keep some information private”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'PTI's drama will never achieve anything': Pak minister Naqvi warns Imran Khan's party ahead of Islamabad march
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan interior minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday warned jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party’s.
articles.body: Pakistan interior minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday warned jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party’s planned protest in Islamabad, saying it “can never achieve anything through such drama."Also Read: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan's sister Aleema arrested in Lahore ahead of Sept 27 PTI marchThe PTI plans to march towards the capital on September 27 to demand the release of its founder Imran Khan, who has been in jail since 2023 after being arrested following his conviction in a corruption case. Currently, the cricketer-turned-politician is lodged at the high-security Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.“We will not allow PTI to enter Islamabad and shut down the city for several days. We have clearly told them that they can never achieve anything through such drama, and I will say again that there is still time; they should not go into this situation,” Naqvi told reporters.He also referred to an Islamabad high court order directing the federal government to ensure peace in the capital and claimed that a majority of PTI leaders did not support the planned protest.“Do not harm yourself and your workers,” he told the PTI leadership, urging it to adopt a “different approach”.Asked about measures to find a long-term solution to the PTI’s repeated protests, Naqvi replied, “This time we will find a permanent solution; we will not leave it halfway. We can't afford this every time.”On reports of a possible ban on the party, he said the government would seek a “once-and-for-all solution.”Meanwhile, the federal government was stepping up security measures ahead of the protest, including placing shipping containers along roads and bringing in police personnel from other provinces.More than 22,000 security personnel, led by eight senior police officers, were to be deployed in Islamabad, while more than 30,000 were to be stationed in Attock district, which connects Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab.Police in Rawalpindi, Islamabad’s twin city, have separately sought 9,000 additional personnel to assist the local administration.The PTI is not the only group planning protests in Islamabad. Right-wing Jamaat-e-Islami launched a demonstration against rising petroleum prices on Sunday and was heading towards the capital from Karachi.The Kissan Ittehad farmers’ group has also announced a sit-in in the city this week, seeking relief for farmers.(With agency inputs)Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Clancy on starting a new family, forgiveness and grief: The key moments from his first interview since the mistrial
articles.summary: Patrick Clancy appeared with his new wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, on '60 Minutes' on Sunday.
articles.body:
Patrick Clancy shared how he has coped with the deaths of his three children and started rebuilding his life in his first televised interview since his ex-wife Lindsay Clancy's murder trial .

The case has drawn widespread media attention, with the former labor and delivery nurse facing murder charges over the deaths of her three children — 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan — whom she admitted killing on Jan. 24, 2023.

In an extensive interview with 60 Minutes aired on CBS News Sunday, Clancy said that at one point he "didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday," as he struggled with grief. He said that he still dreams about his children, telling interviewer Ross Douthat, "it's like I'm lucid in those dreams."

Clancy also discussed how he met his now-wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, who also appeared in the show, and said false online conspiracy theories about his involvement in his children's deaths were "deeply harmful to the legacy of my children."

Here are the key moments from the interview.

1. He and his new wife are starting a family

Asked by correspondent Ross Douthat whether the couple were "starting a family" together, Danis replied, "Yeah," with Clancy adding that he "can't wait" to tell any future children child about their brothers and sister.

"I think every parent can agree, you have different relationships with your kids, but they're all your kids," he said. "And I can't wait to tell them about their brothers and sister."

Danis, a fertility doctor, married Clancy in April this year. Joining her husband for the interview, she said that she first met him at a running club in New York in January 2024.

She described finding out about his children while paying for coffee with Clancy during one of their meet-ups.

"Pat pulled out his phone to pay, and I noticed this adorable photo of children as the wallpaper," she said. "And I just asked, 'Who are those cuties?' And Pat said, 'Those are my kids.' And then I think I asked if they live in Massachusetts, and Pat said, 'They died.' And this is just at the cashier."

"I guess I had so many questions, and yet at the same time I didn't know exactly what to ask," she added.

Clancy, who was the first witness to testify at his ex-wife's murder trial, told the court that when he returned from picking up food and prescriptions, he found his three children in the basement after calling 911 for Lindsay, who had jumped from a second-floor window.

During the 60 Minutes special, he described having a panic attack mid-testimony and being put in an ambulance.

"I went to a back room, and I started having this massive traumatic panic attack," he said.

"My heart was pounding. And they put me in an ambulance. They offered me some medication, but I said, 'I — I don't want it, 'cause I want to go back and I want to finish this so I can be done with this.' And I went back and I finished the testimony."

Recalling the 911 call being played in court, he said that "testifying is very difficult."

"On the second day, a lot of that was focused on the night of January 24th. We did take a break right before they played the 911 call, which I knew was gonna be just horrific."

The account rebuts what some online theorists interpreted as Clancy's stoicism on the stand, which in turn fueled conspiracy theories that he was somehow involved in the deaths of his children. These theories continued even after Clancy's lawyer warned he would take legal action against those responsible.

Asked about the impact of the conspiracy theories circulating online , Clancy said, "It's painful to see. It makes it difficult to be in public, and it's possible that some of those people, after seeing lie after lie after lie, they start to believe it, and that's what we're left with."

He said that the conspiracy theories are "deeply harmful to the legacy of my children."

"It is a huge distraction from what really matters here, which is perinatal mental health. And it's done real harm to real people, myself included but also others," he added.

4. He didn't expect to survive his own grief — and forgave his ex-wife

While Patrick and Lindsay Clancy are no longer married, Patrick Clancy told CBS he had forgiven his ex-wife for what happened to their children.

Asked if she had ever asked for his forgiveness, Clancy said, "No. But I gave it to her."

"I saw headlines that said, you know, 'Killer Mom,' and 'Baby Murderer,' 'Monster.' And none of 'em were accurate. I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that. So I shared those words.

"And I think when it comes to forgiveness, I also felt that if I didn't get there, I would be eaten up inside forever," he added.

In the weeks following the tragedy, as Clancy tried to come to terms with life without his children, he discussed feeling so low that he had suicidal thoughts.

"There was a time when I — I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday. And I was completely fine with it," he told the broadcaster.

Two of the Clancys' children — Cora and Dawson — were declared dead on Jan. 24, but 8-month-old Callan remained alive for a few more days after being airlifted to Boston Children's Hospital.

"I really thought there was a chance that Callan would live," he told 60 Minutes.

"I remember just thinking, 'Just gimme one. Just gimme one kid,' and I would raise him as best I could, and I would give him the best life I possibly could. I'd tell him about his brother and sister. And I was holding out hope for that.

"Then, when I got to the hospital, I saw the doctor. I saw the look on her face, and I knew that it wasn't going to be a good prognosis."

During his final hours with Callan, Clancy said he sat and wrote tributes to each of his three children, typing with one hand while he held his baby's hand with the other. He told the program that he was afraid that if he didn't write about them, they would be forgotten.

Callan's heart kept beating for four days before "he died in my arms," Clancy said.

"I'm so grateful for those four days that I had with him. And I'm so grateful he hung on," he said.

If you or someone you know is experiencing suicidal thoughts, call 911, or call the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-8255 or text HOME to the Crisis Text Line at 741741.

articles.title: 'Deeply ashamed, Bihar in grips of gunda-raj': Tejashwi targets BJP govt over Jamui harassment case
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Bihar Assembly Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Monday condemned the alleged harassment of a boy and a girl in Jamui, describing the .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bihar Assembly Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Monday condemned the alleged harassment of a boy and a girl in Jamui, describing the incident as "truly tragic" and expressing concern over the safety of women in the state."We are deeply ashamed. The government, however, seems to have lost all sense of shame or decency regarding such events," Yadav said, referring to the viral video of the incident.While talking to the reporters he questioned the safety of girls in Bihar, alleging that incidents of atrocities against women were increasing across the state."Whether it is day or night; whether at college, school, on the street, in a hostel, or even inside or outside their homes—the rise in atrocities against women in Bihar is undeniable," he said.Yadav also alleged that the government and police focus on suppressing such cases instead of ensuring justice for victims. "It is utterly shameful. A state of lawlessness—gunda-raj—has completely taken hold in Bihar," he said.Jamui Police has launched an investigation after videos allegedly showing the harassment of a girl by a group of youths surfaced on social media. The videos purportedly show the girl being stopped on the road, subjected to inappropriate physical contact and allegedly dragged. Police have arrested three and registered an FIR after taking cognisance of the viral footage.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2013, Pink paid nearly $9 million for a 200-acre California ranch with a 10,000-sq-ft home; 13 years later, the estate has become a working organic vineyard producing her Two Wolves wine
articles.summary: US News: Singer Alecia Beth Moore-Hart, known professionally as Pink, bought a 200-acre ranch in California’s Santa Barbara County with her husband Carey Hart .
articles.body: Singer Alecia Beth Moore-Hart, known professionally as Pink, bought a 200-acre ranch in California’s Santa Barbara County with her husband Carey Hart in 2013 for almost $9 million. The property included a vineyard. Thirteen years later, the land is also home to Two Wolves Wine, the label she created after spending years learning about winemaking and organic farming.The purchase came while wine was still a growing interest for Pink, Forbes reported. She found the property online while she was on tour in Australia and bought it without seeing it herself. She sent Hart to look at it before the purchase. The couple had already been visiting the Santa Ynez area for about 20 years, riding motorcycles and stopping at wineries along the way. According to Realtor, apart from the vineyard, the property included a 10-bedroom, 10,000-square-foot estate, a pool and a spa.Pink's interest in wine had started much earlier. She told Forbes that she did not grow up drinking wine and once thought it was 'punishment at holiday dinners'. That changed in her 20s, when people in her management team introduced her to better wines and wineries while she was on tour. She began visiting vineyards during breaks from performances and later studied about it through Wine and Spirit Educational Trust courses and UCLA Extension.Pink eventually began learning about the work that goes into producing it, including farming grapes and caring for the land. While touring for her concerts, she continued her studies backstage. She would finish performances and then open her laptop to study wine. Her interest in wineries also took her to places such as Penfolds and Clos Rougeard, where she learned from winemakers and asked questions about their methods.Learning to make wineAfter buying the California property, Pink began making wine herself. She initially worked on small batches in a refrigerated garage, starting with a single macro bin. She was not planning to release the wine commercially at first. Instead, she was making it because she wanted to learn.Winemaker Alison Thomson later became her partner and co-winemaker. The two met at a dinner party, which Pink described as a kind of 'stealth dinner party interview'. Thomson did not know she was being considered for the role at the time. She eventually joined Pink in developing the wines.Pink's first vintage was made in 2014. She kept the project largely private for several years before deciding to release the wine. The first Two Wolves bottling finally came out in 2018.At the time, Pink said she was concerned that people in the wine industry might not take her seriously because she was a celebrity. "I was worried that people would think I was a clown." She said she did not want to simply put her name on a bottle made by someone else. "I really rolled up my sleeves," she said.Why organic farming became centralOrganic farming is a major part of the Two Wolves project. The vineyard Pink bought was certified organic, and she has continued to make that approach central to the operation.Pink explained her concern about the use of pesticides by pointing to the possible risks for vineyard workers. "You hear horror stories of a vineyard worker that got cut with pesticides in his leg, and now he's an amputee. Real stories," she said.Thomson, who studied restorative ecology before working in wine, also described the vineyard as a complete system. The team uses cover crops, which are plants grown to help support soil and the wider vineyard environment. It also has native plantings, owl boxes and bluebird boxes.Thomson said the aim is to maintain healthy soil with good drainage and nutrients. These factors matter because grapevines depend on the soil in which they grow, while the plants and animals around them form part of the wider vineyard ecosystem.The wines are grown on 25 certified-organic acres in Santa Barbara County. This is part of the larger 200-acre ranch that Pink and Hart bought in 2013.Building Two WolvesThe winery's name comes from a teaching story about two wolves living inside a person. One represents qualities such as greed, envy, anger, jealousy, selfishness and fear, while the other represents curiosity, compassion, generosity and love. When asked which wolf wins, the answer is, "The one you feed."Pink said she has always known the story as a Cherokee legend, while noting that the Two Wolves property sits on Chumash land. For her, the story represents balance and the choices people make.The winery has also become a project led by women. Pink built the Two Wolves team with five women. Thomson said the project gave her an opportunity to continue working in wine while also having space for family life.Pink said she had never had a female mentor before working on Two Wolves. She described the experience of working with women in charge as different from what she had known earlier in her career.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Protests erupt in Texas after ICE officer shoots Venezuelan man, DHS says he was in US illegally
articles.summary: US News: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot and wounded a 28-year-old Venezuelan man during a law enforcement operation in Austin, Texas.
articles.body: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot and wounded a 28-year-old Venezuelan man during a law enforcement operation in Austin, Texas, on Sunday, triggering protests at the scene against the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown.The man, identified as Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, was shot in the torso and taken to a hospital in serious but stable condition, according to officials. His lawyer said Garcés Pérez had arrived in the US from Venezuela about two years ago and was working as a DoorDash delivery driver when he encountered ICE agents.DHS says Venezuelan man had final removal orderThe Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from the FBI, is leading the investigation into the shooting. DHS said the Venezuelan man had entered the US illegally under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal. The agency said he was in stable condition and remained in federal custody pending removal.Austin police were not involved in the operation or the shooting, according to Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis. Local officers arrived after the shooting and provided first aid to the wounded man.Protests erupt at Austin shooting sceneDozens of protesters gathered near the scene, with some carrying Mexican and Guatemalan flags and signs demanding that ICE leave Austin.The Guardian reported that the crowd grew to about 100 people as a large law enforcement presence remained in the area.Texas Congressman Greg Casar called for a full and immediate investigation and demanded the release of body-camera footage. The shooting comes amid heightened scrutiny of ICE operations across the US following several shootings involving immigration agents.The Trump administration has defended its expanded immigration enforcement campaign as necessary for public safety and for carrying out its promise of increased deportations.The circumstances that led to the shooting remained unclear. Austin Mayor Kirk Watson called for transparency and said the city should be involved in the investigation, while local officials and lawmakers called for an independent probe.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2020, a New Jersey man lost his job and began mowing lawns for free; six years later, his volunteer network has grown to more than 2,000 people across all 50 US states
articles.summary: US News: In 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted daily life in the US, Brian Schwartz lost his job. Landscape Management reported that Schwartz, who was .
articles.body: In 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted daily life in the US, Brian Schwartz lost his job. Landscape Management reported that Schwartz, who was also caring for a sick parent at the time, found a way to help older neighbours and veterans struggling to maintain their yards.What started as a simple act of help soon attracted people who wanted to do the same. Schwartz created a basic website with his contact details so people could reach him. Requests began coming from outside his neighbourhood, and volunteers started contacting him to ask how they could help people in their own communities, the organisation's webiste says.That small effort eventually became I Want To Mow Your Lawn, a registered nonprofit based in Wayne, New Jersey. The organisation now connects volunteers with older adults, veterans and other people who need temporary help with their yards. It operates through volunteers rather than as a paid landscaping service.Six years after Schwartz started with a mower and a small group of volunteers, the network has expanded to more than 2,000 volunteers across all 50 US states. Its website currently lists more than 2,060 actively enlisted volunteers, over 3,090 service visits and more than 630 households served. It also says more than 15,000 people have reached out for help.A nationwide networkThe organisation says it began in the summer of 2020 with 10 volunteers and a borrowed lawn mower. The idea was simply to connect people who could not manage their lawns with people willing to give their time and equipment to help them.Schwartz said the response went beyond what he expected. In a note on the organisation's website, he recalled how requests first came from beyond his neighbourhood and then beyond New Jersey.The organisation says its purpose is not to replace professional landscaping services. Instead, it provides temporary lawn-care relief through volunteers.The service can include mowing, raking, trimming and edging. Some volunteers also provide other outdoor help. The organisation says there is no charge for the people receiving the service and that donations are optional.Volunteers decide when to helpThe network is built around individual volunteers rather than a traditional landscaping workforce. Once approved, volunteers can use the organisation's website or app to find requests near them.They can see information about the work required, the distance and preferred dates before deciding whether to take a visit. Volunteers are not required to make a long-term commitment and can choose individual visits.The organisation says volunteers communicate with homeowners through privacy-protected channels. After completing a visit, they can record their hours and upload before-and-after photographs.The organisation also reviews volunteers before approving them. It describes itself as a facilitator rather than a contractor and says coverage can vary depending on where volunteers are available.More than 3,000 lawn-care visitsThe numbers show how far the original idea has expanded. The organisation's current website lists more than 2,060 volunteers, 3,090 service visits and 630 unique households served. It says volunteers are active across all 50 states.It also says more than 9,000 people had contacted the organisation for help through its online form and voicemail line in one of its current impact updates. The requests come from people who may be older, veterans, living with disabilities or dealing with financial or physical difficulties that make yard work harder.For Schwartz, the response from volunteers became an important part of the project. He wrote that some volunteers told him that helping a stranger had changed their week or their outlook.“We were doing what we could to provide some relief at a difficult time. One thing led to another with people starting to reach out- homeowners, volunteers,” Schwartz said, as qouted by MLB.com.Yankees recognised the organisationThe nonprofit received wider attention in 2026 when the Major League Baseball teamNew York Yankees selected Schwartz and I Want To Mow Your Lawn for the team's HOPE week.During the June 2026 event, Yankees players, coaches and staff joined Schwartz and volunteers in New Jersey to work on a homeowner's yard. The group included Yankees general manager Brian Cashman, who helped with the yard work, along with players and coaches.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Russia has lost control': Trump flags diesel crisis, calls for end to 'ridiculous' Ukraine war
articles.summary: US News: US president Donald Trump has again pressed Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, linking the attacks to .
articles.body: US president Donald Trump has again pressed Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, linking the attacks to a tightening global diesel market and rising fuel prices. He also renewed his call for an end to what he described as a “ridiculous and never-ending” war.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said on Monday that Russia had “lost control” of its diesel industry as a result of the war, claiming that several refineries had been damaged.have been blown up and are, at least temporarily, out of commission.“Russia has unfortunately lost control of its Diesel Oil Industry due to its War with Ukraine. A large number of their Diesel refineries have been blown up and are, at least temporarily, out of commission,” Trump said in the post.He added, “This ridiculous and never ending War with Ukraine must be ended. The whole World suffers as 25,000 people, mostly soldiers, are being killed each month. What a shame! President DJT”The remarks came a day before Trump was due to meet Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Zelenskyy said after Sunday's call that it had been an “important conversation” and that his meeting with Trump “could change a lot”. His office said the two leaders were expected to meet on Tuesday.According to the Financial Times, Trump’s central message during the call was “diesel, diesel . . . diesel”. A senior Ukrainian official who participated in the conversation told the newspaper that Trump urged Zelenskyy to order his military to stop drone and missile attacks on Russian refineries.Another senior Ukrainian official familiar with the call told the FT that Trump was “very worried” about rising diesel prices and wanted Russian supplies to reach global markets.Trump had made a similar appeal publicly on September 13, saying, “Mr. Zelenskiy has to do one thing: He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia.” He added: “There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel. That's hurting the world.”The Kremlin welcomed Trump’s appeal. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow could only welcome any call for Kyiv to stop attacks on civilian economic infrastructure. He also said Russia’s view was that the disruption in global energy markets was being driven largely by instability and renewed escalation in the Gulf region.Ukraine has defended attacks on Russian refineries as legitimate military targets, while a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes has reduced Russian refining output and contributed to fuel shortages. Reuters reported last week that six major diesel-producing refineries had suffered significant production cuts or shutdowns in September.The latest call followed what Russian authorities described as the largest-ever drone attack on Moscow, during which a major oil refinery was reportedly set ablaze. The Kremlin has previously welcomed Trump's calls for Ukraine to stop attacks on Russian diesel facilities.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Father diamond businessman in Gujarat, mother runs NGO: Redditor with Rs 49 LPA salary denied F-1 visa for Harvard MBA, says paid agent Rs 5 lakh for appointment
articles.summary: US News: A Redditor has shared a detailed account of how she was refused an F-1 visa, though she claimed to have got through Harvard for her MBA. The authentic.
articles.body: A Redditor has shared a detailed account of how she was refused an F-1 visa, though she claimed to have got through Harvard for her MBA. The authenticity of the Reddit post is not independently verified but several details of the post raised many questions starting with the amount the Redditor claimed to have paid to an agent to ger the appointment. "I booked my visa slot through an agent and paid an absolutely ridiculous amount (~5Lakhs). He managed to get me the appointment," the person said.The interview was at the US Embassy, New Delhi and there were a lot of rejections before her, including someone who was going to NYU Stern for an MBA.Why leave your job for an MBA?The Redditor said she was asked the basic questions and was also congratulate by the visa officer for getting selected for Harvard. The Redditor said she is a consultant at a Big-4 firm and earns Rs 49 LPA salary. The visa officer asked her why she would be leaving her high-paying job to pursue an MBA."I don’t see the MBA as leaving my career behind. It’s more of an investment in the next stage of it. My current role has given me strong analytical and consulting experience, but I want to build the management and leadership side of my skill set as well. I think the MBA will help me make that transition," the Redditor said to the visa officer, adding that her father is a diamond businessman in Gujarat and her mother runs an NGO in Jamnagar and she wanted to join the family business eventually -- no plan to settle in the US.The Redditor was also asked about her travel history, which included 18 countries, and she also had a valid B1/B2 visa for the US."Unfortunately, you do not qualify for a US visa," the visa officer said and also canceled her existing B1/B2 visa with a stamp saying: "Cancelled without prejudice".Social media users pointed out that paying Rs 5 lakh to an agent to get an appointment was enough of a red flag in this particular case. Many doubted whether this actually happened or just a fake post as they questioned that a Big-4 consultant with such a high salary in India does not need a Harvard MBA to join the family business."If I need Harvard or not, that’s honestly my problem. If I get into Harvard and i’m able to get in, I’ll go, simple as that. I don’t really see the point in speculating about whether i “need” an MBA or whether the family business needs it. that’s a personal decision and it doesn’t really have anything to do with the visa," the Redditor said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
